Riemann Dynamics · 20265B

Causal DiT with 3D re-projected patch memory

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Matrix-Game 3.5 distills a bidirectional world model into a few-step fully causal generator and keeps long-term memory as geometry: historical VAE-latent patches are lifted to 3D with metric depth, re-projected into the target view and inserted as tokens of one pose-aware sequence. Each 3-latent-frame chunk attends causally to a clean anchor, the preceding chunks, one chunk-local context frame and its patch memory; third-person models add multi-view reference tokens for the controlled character. Camera pose enters through tiled PRoPE with no new parameters. A 3-step causal student reaches up to 20 fps at 1280x704 on one H100 with INT8, GPU retrieval and a 75%-pruned decoder (company claim).

Representation

Wan2.2 VAE 4x16x16 → 44x80x48 latent per latent frame at 1280x704; 2x2 patchify (Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config) → 22x40 = 880 tokens per latent frame, 2,640 per 3-latent chunk of 12 frames [D]; 48 latent channels

Core

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT: 30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336 (HF config); the full DiT is fine-tuned with the text encoder and VAE frozen; the only learnable additions are the reference-token embeddings

Attention

Block-causal chunks of 3 latent frames: the chunk's 2,640 queries attend to a rolling KV window (clean anchor + ≤6 previous chunks = ≤19 latent frames, released config), 1 chunk-local context frame, 3 frames of patch memory (≤1 token per target cell) and itself: ≤26 latent frames ≈ 22,880 K/V tokens per chunk [D]; causal training window 1 anchor + 7 chunks = 22 positions; the paper's ≈2.3x sequence bound is for the bidirectional base model's 21-frame sample

Actions

Camera pose via tiled PRoPE in every block: after RoPE, queries × Pᵀ, keys and values × P⁻¹, outputs × P, tiled over all head channels, no new parameters; translations recentred on the first target frame and log-compressed

Prediction

Perceptual flow matching causal adaptation (10k steps), then curriculum self-rollout DMD (1,000 outer steps, 5:1 update ratio) → 3-step causal generator; prefix and chunk-local context held at the next noise level each substep (HiAR), anchor clean

Decoder

MG-LightVAE, 75%-pruned Wan2.2 decoder → 12 frames per chunk at 1280x704; 'VAE decoding becomes the primary latency bottleneck' once the DiT is accelerated

Memory

Patch memory (MosaicMem-style): patches lifted to 3D with metric depth and poses, frustum-queried, z-buffered and scattered into a target-aligned memory frame; retrieval runs for every generated chunk (on GPU, inside the real-time loop), and each chunk is decoded and registered before the next query; only the dynamic-object filter runs once per segment, outside the denoising loop; the memory bank grows with rollout length, the per-chunk sequence does not

Speed

Up to 20 output frames/s at 1280x704, batch 1, one H100, including the INT8 3-step DiT, online retrieval and MG-LightVAE decode (company claim; the VLM prompt rewriter runs asynchronously); undistilled model in the SANA-WM benchmark: 10.9 one-minute videos/hour at 77.0 GB peak, #G = 1, measured on an 8xH100 node (authors' Table 1)

Key detail

Long-term memory is geometric (patch memory); short-term context is a bounded rolling KV window (anchor + ≤6 chunks), so per-chunk DiT cost stops growing once the window fills [D]; memory retrieval runs every chunk on the real-time path, and only the dynamic-object filter is amortised per segment

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (technical report). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2608.29910 Sec. 2.1 (tiled PRoPE), 2.2 (patch, context and reference memory), 2.3 (distillation), 4.1 (implementation), 4.4 (real-time inference), Table 1; HF Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (30 layers, dim 3072, 24 heads, ffn 14336, 48 latent channels); Wan2.2 README (VAE 4x16x16); Official code github.com/Riemann-Dynamics/Matrix-Game-3.5 (model_configs.py, wan_video_dit.py, causal_rollout.py rolling KV window, configs/infer_distilled_6blocks.yaml); weights HF RiemannDynamics/Matrix-Game-3.5-Base and -Distilled.

NVIDIA · 202616B Nano

Reasoner and generator towers share one attention

World-actionread

Details
Overview

An omnimodal world model built as a mixture of transformers: a reasoner tower (initialized from Qwen3-VL, then further pre-trained and fine-tuned) runs autoregressively over text and ViT tokens, and a generator tower denoises video latents, audio and action tokens with flow matching. The towers keep their own norms, attention projections and MLPs but share one self-attention operator, so every diffusion token can read the AR context. One set of weights serves generation, forward and inverse dynamics and a policy, selected by which tokens are clean and which are noisy; the post-trained DROID policy runs 4 steps with CFG split across 2 RTX Pro 6000 GPUs and skips video decoding.

Representation

Generation: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B VAE latents, 4x temporal and 32x32 spatial (16x16 VAE + 2x2 patch merge), linearly projected to the hidden size, so ⌈H/32⌉ x ⌈W/32⌉ tokens per latent frame, e.g. 23 x 40 = 920 at 720p 16:9, because an odd latent side is zero-padded before the merge [D]; understanding: ViT tokens (patch 16, 2x2 merge); audio 25 tokens/s (48 kHz, hop 1920)

Core

Nano: 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads / 8 KV heads of 128, FFN 12,288 in each of two towers = 16B (from Qwen3-VL-8B); Super: 64 layers, hidden 5120, 64 / 8 heads, FFN 25,600 = 64B; Edge 4B (28 layers, hidden 2048) released 20 Jul 2026

Attention

Shared self-attention: AR tokens attend causally to AR tokens only; DM tokens attend bidirectionally over all AR + DM tokens; AR tokens never read DM tokens; training packs a fixed 74,000-token context

Actions

Action vectors (relative ego pose 9-D, effector pose 9-D, grasp state; 10-D single arm up to 57-D egocentric human) enter as DM tokens through per-embodiment input and output projections; the MoT backbone is shared; the DROID policy re-initializes the action encoder, decoding MLP and action embedding tokens

Prediction

Flow matching: 50 steps for generation (guidance 6, shift 10), 4 steps for the DROID policy (guidance 3, shift 5) predicting 32 absolute joint-position actions at 15 Hz; the reasoner pass is computed once and cached across all steps; σ enters as a sinusoidal timestep embedding (256 → Linear-SiLU-Linear) added to every noisy video, audio and action token after its input projection, with no AdaLN in the layers (code)

Decoder

Wan2.2 VAE decoder for video; skipped in policy serving, where only the action tokens are read

Memory

The report describes no streaming rollout; the Nano model card chains 16-frame forward-dynamics chunks, each re-conditioned on the previous chunk's last generated frame. Within each sample the generator attends bidirectionally over its AR + DM tokens; paged KV caching only for reasoner serving (TensorRT-LLM / vLLM)

Speed

Nano 720p text-to-video on one GPU: 297 s on H100 NVL vs 115 s on B200 (PyTorch; frames and steps not stated); policy served on 2 RTX Pro 6000 with CFG parallelism, per-chunk latency not disclosed (company claims)

Key detail

Each token passes through one tower, so per-token compute stays near the dense 8B backbone while total parameters grow ≈1.8x (15.75B vs 8.77B) [D]; the DROID policy runs 4 steps x a 540x640 three-view canvas and skips decoding the video latents

Status and sources

company technical report. Availability: code + weights. Sources: Cosmos 3 technical report (22 Jun 2026) Sec. 2.1 (encoders, action tokenization), Sec. 2.3 (MoT, attention), Table 2 (variants), Sec. 4.2 (74K context), Sec. 5 (reasoner caching, CFG parallelism, Fig. 16 timings), Sec. 4.2.5 (DROID policy: 4 steps, 2 RTX Pro 6000, decoding skipped), Table 21 (sampler settings); NVIDIA/cosmos-framework (commit 300faa14): cosmos_framework/model/vfm/mot/unified_mot.py (RMSNorm, per-tower layers), cosmos3_vfm_network.py (patch padding, timestep embedding); Hugging Face model cards and configs: nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano, Cosmos3-Edge, Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID.

NVIDIA · 20262.6B

Hybrid linear DiT with a fixed-size state

State-spaceread

Details
Overview

A minute-scale camera-controlled world model whose DiT replaces most softmax attention with frame-wise Gated DeltaNet: 15 of 20 blocks keep a D×D recurrent state per head, updated once per latent frame, and only 5 blocks use softmax attention, run at deployment with an attention sink plus a local window. The LTX2 VAE packs 8 raw frames into one 128-channel latent frame, so 60 s of 720p fits one GPU. Self Forcing distillation gives a 4-step chunk-causal generator; with NVFP4 on one RTX 5090 it denoises 60 s of 720p in 34 s (authors).

Representation

LTX2 VAE, 128 latent channels, one latent frame per 8 raw frames; spatial stride and tokens per latent frame at 720p are not stated in the paper, which calls the representation 8x smaller than Wan2.1-VAE's

Core

Hybrid linear DiT from SANA-Video: 20 blocks, d 2240, 20 heads of 112; 15 frame-wise Gated DeltaNet blocks + softmax attention at layers {3, 7, 11, 15, 19}, keeping the original QKV and output projections; text, video and pose tokens pass through the alternating blocks; LayerNorm (no affine) + adaLN-single shift/scale/gate on the attention and FFN sub-layers, cross-attention without norm (released code)

Attention

GDN blocks: a D×D recurrent state per head updated once per latent frame from all S spatial tokens (forward scan global, reversed scan reset at chunk boundaries in the chunk-causal variant); softmax blocks: first latent frame as sink + local temporal window at deployment; chunk = 3 latent frames (first chunk 4), deployment window = sink + 2 cached chunks (released config and CLI)

Actions

6-DoF camera trajectory only (the CLI's WASD/IJKL keys are rolled out to a trajectory): UCPE relative camera encoding on the geometric channels of a camera attention branch at latent-frame rate, plus the 8 raw-frame Plücker raymaps of one VAE stride packed into a 48-channel tensor through a zero-initialized 3D patch embedder; applied in every block

Prediction

Flow matching; 60-step chunk-causal AR generator distilled with Self Forcing to 4 steps; bidirectional, chunk-causal and distilled variants each run on one GPU

Decoder

LTX2 VAE decoder → 720p at 16 fps (961 frames = 60 s [D]); optional second stage: LTX-2 17B refiner with a rank-384 LoRA, 3 Euler steps

Memory

15 GDN layers each hold a main and a camera-branch D×D state per head plus a D-vector normalizer: 2 × 20 × 112² + 20 × 112 = 504,000 fp32 values ≈ 2.0 MB per layer, ≈30 MB for all 15 [D]; the 5 softmax layers keep a sink + window KV, so memory is constant in rollout length (all-softmax runs out of memory at 60 s on an H100, Fig. 7b); no explicit 3D scene memory

Speed

60 s of 720p: DiT time on one H100 21.7 min at 60 steps → 43 s at 4 steps → 29 s with the sink (34 s end to end); 34 s DiT on one RTX 5090 with NVFP4, 42 s with the 7.3 s VAE decode (authors, Fig. 7a); 433 ms per denoising step at 720p on one H100, 5.68 GiB (Table 3, 5 s clips); 24.1 one-minute videos per hour on 8 H100s (Table 2)

Key detail

At deployment, per-chunk cost is constant in rollout length in all 20 layers (GDN state in 15, sink + local-window KV in 5); the VAE swap is the bigger lever per step (3.4x latency, 8.9 → 5.4 GiB, while also going from 480p to 720p); replacing cumulative linear attention with hybrid GDN + softmax costs 1.17x per step (433.2 vs 371.7 ms) and raises memory from 5.40 to 5.68 GiB [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2605.15178 abstract, Sec. 1, 3.1 (stages), 3.2 (frame-wise GDN, hybrid), 3.3 (UCPE + Plücker mixing), 5.1 (backbone), 5.4 and Fig. 7 (speed path), Tables 2-3, App. C.1 (head dim 112); NVlabs/Sana code: sana_multi_scale_video_camctrl.py, sana_gdn_camctrl_blocks.py, fused_streaming.py, inference_sana_wm_streaming.py, sana_wm_streaming_1600m_720p.yaml; HF model card (CLI --action).

Skywork AI · 20265B nominal

Bidirectional segment DiT with retrieved memory

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Skywork's 720p successor to Matrix-Game 2.0, built on Wan2.2-TI2V-5B. Unlike its predecessor it keeps a bidirectional DiT: each streaming segment denoises 10 new latent frames jointly with 4 past latents and 5 memory latents retrieved by camera pose and frustum overlap, all in one self-attention sequence with no KV cache. Multi-segment DMD distils it to 3 steps. The reported ~40 FPS at 720p needs 8 GPUs for the DiT plus 1 for the VAE, INT8 attention projections, a 75%-pruned decoder and GPU-side retrieval (company claim).

Representation

Wan2.2 VAE (4x16x16) + 1x2x2 patchify; a 704x1280 frame becomes a 44x80 latent and a 22x40 grid of 880 tokens per latent frame [D]; one latent frame = 4 video frames (the first latent holds 1); 10 latent frames per segment = 40 video frames (first segment 57)

Core

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336 per the HF config); action modules in the first 15 blocks as in Matrix-Game 2.0; teacher and student share one bidirectional architecture; a 28B MoE scale-up is also trained

Attention

Bidirectional within a segment: 5 retrieved memory latents + 4 past latents + 10 noisy current latents in one sequence (first segment: reference latent + 14 noisy latents), ≈16,720 tokens per segment [D]; head-wise perturbed RoPE bases; no KV cache

Actions

Keyboard actions through a dedicated cross-attention module, mouse signals through self-attention (Matrix-Game 2.0 design), in blocks 1-15; relative Plücker cues encode the camera geometry between the target and the retrieved memory; in every block a Plücker-driven scale/shift (four 3072x3072 layers per block; camera layers total ≈1.17B params in the checkpoint [D]) modulates the tokens after self-attention

Prediction

Flow matching; multi-segment self-rollout DMD (1-6 segments, memory from an online pool) → 3 distilled steps per segment; error collection and injection train the model on its own imperfect histories

Decoder

MG-LightVAE: Wan2.2 decoder with reduced hidden widths (LightX2V-style), 50% or 75% pruned; decode 0.76 → 0.30 → 0.13 s per 17-frame 720x1280 clip (PSNR 33.79 → 31.84 → 31.14 dB); runs on its own GPU

Memory

Camera-aware retrieval: each query view takes the past frame with the highest frustum-overlap score (exact on CPU, approximate on GPU); the first latent can be kept as a persistent sink; without a KV cache the memory and past tokens are re-processed at every step

Speed

~40 FPS at 720p on an asynchronous 8+1 pipeline (8 DiT GPUs + 1 VAE GPU); GPU model not named (results cover H-series with FlashAttention 3 and A-series with FlashAttention 2); leave-one-out Table 1: 27.38 FPS without INT8, 25.79 without MG-LightVAE, 6.60 with CPU retrieval; single-node 7+1 'slightly lower' (company claim); 3.1 one-minute videos/hour on 8 H100s in SANA-WM's benchmark (third party; Matrix-Game 3.0's multi-step, undistilled AR setting, not the 3-step real-time pipeline); the ~40 FPS figure is a company claim

Key detail

Real time is a systems result: 9 GPUs, INT8 on the attention projections only (+46% [D]), a decoder the authors report as up to 5.2x faster (Table 2 decode times imply ≈5.8x [D]) (+55% [D]) and GPU retrieval (≈6.1x [D]); the authors say VAE decode is the bottleneck once the DiT is optimized

Status and sources

company technical report (arXiv), v3 Sep 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2604.08995 Sec. 3.1 (base model, action injection), 3.2 (memory), 3.3 (multi-segment DMD), 3.4 and Tables 1-2 (real-time inference, MG-LightVAE), 5.1 (implementation), 5.2.3 (throughput); Official code SkyworkAI/Matrix-Game (Matrix-Game-3): wan/configs/config.py, wan/modules/model.py, wan/modules/action_module.py, pipeline/inference_interactive_pipeline.py; HF checkpoint config.json; HF Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (30 layers, dim 3072, 24 heads, ffn 14336); SANA-WM arXiv 2605.15178 Sec. 5.2, Table 2 (3.1 videos/hour on 8 H100s).

Mila, NYU · 2026~18M total

One token per frame, CEM plans in under a second

Embedding predictorread

Details
Overview

The smallest JEPA world model in the gallery: a ViT-Tiny encoder and a 6-layer predictor trained end to end from pixels with two losses only (next-embedding MSE plus the SIGReg Gaussian regularizer), with no EMA, stop-gradient or frozen foundation encoder. Each frame is squeezed into a single 192-d [CLS] embedding, so the predictor sees at most 3 tokens, and a CEM plan of 300 samples x up to 30 iterations x horizon 5 finishes in 0.98 s against 47 s for DINO-WM.

Representation

One 192-d token per 224x224 frame: the last-layer [CLS] embedding of a ViT-Tiny (patch 14, 12 layers, 3 heads, width 192, ~5M) followed by a 1-layer MLP projector with BatchNorm

Core

Predictor: 6 layers, d 192, 16 heads of 64, MLP 2048, dropout 0.1, learned positional embeddings; ~10M; followed by a projector of the same design as the encoder's

Attention

Temporal causal mask over the history of frame embeddings; N = 3 frames (paper: 1 for TwoRoom; the released TwoRoom checkpoint and code use 3), i.e. at most 3 tokens per predictor call [D]

Actions

Zero-initialised AdaLN at every predictor layer; with frameskip 5 the 5 actions between frames form one 10-d action block, embedded to width 192

Prediction

One pass regresses the next frame embedding (MSE); encoder and predictor trained jointly, SIGReg keeps the embeddings Gaussian to prevent collapse

Decoder

None in training or planning; a diagnostic cross-attention decoder (196 queries → 224x224) only visualizes what the latent retains

Memory

Window of N = 3 frame embeddings; no KV cache

Speed

Full plan 0.98 s vs 47 s for DINO-WM, averaged over 50 runs (authors; GPU not stated); CEM with 300 samples, top 30, up to 30 iterations (PushT) or 10, horizon 5 latent steps = 25 environment steps, whole plan executed before replanning

Key detail

196x fewer tokens per frame than DINO-WM [D]; a PushT plan is 150 sequential batched calls (30 iterations x 5 predictor steps), each over 300 candidates with windows of 1, 2, 3, 3, 3 tokens: ~7-21 GFLOP per call, ~2.5 TFLOP per plan [D], a latency-bound chain rather than a throughput job

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v3 Jun 2026). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2603.19312 Sec. 3 (architecture, planning), Sec. 4.2 and Fig. 3 (timing), App. D (encoder, predictor, decoder, planning solver); Hugging Face quentinll/lewm-pusht config.json (predictor d 192, head dim 64, MLP 2048, history 3); GitHub lucas-maes/le-wm README, module.py, jepa.py, config/eval/solver/cem.yaml; Hugging Face quentinll/lewm-pusht and lewm-tworooms weights.pt (parameter count).

Tsinghua IIIS, Galaxea AI · 20266B

Video DiT plus action expert, no imagined video

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A mixture-of-transformers world-action model that keeps video co-training but drops test-time imagination. A Wan2.2-5B video DiT and a 1B action-expert DiT (the same architecture at d 1024) share attention; in training, future video latents and the action chunk are denoised jointly under a structured mask, while at inference the video DiT runs once over the clean first-frame tokens and the action expert denoises a 32-step chunk in 10 steps. That gives 190 ms per chunk on one RTX 5090D against 810 ms for the Fast-WAM-IDM variant.

Representation

Wan2.2 VAE latents of the observation, with the multi-camera images concatenated into one image; training video chunks of 9 frames after 4x temporal downsampling; 98 tokens per latent frame on LIBERO (224x448 input) and 120 on RoboTwin (384x320) [D from released config]; a proprioceptive-state token joins the T5 context (code)

Core

Video DiT from Wan2.2-5B (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14,336 per its config.json) plus an action expert with the same architecture at d 1024 (1B); T5 text reaches all tokens through cross-attention; norms and timestep modulation not detailed in the paper

Attention

Shared attention with a structured mask: clean first-frame tokens attend to nothing else; future video tokens (training only) attend within the video branch and to the first frame; action tokens attend within the action branch and to the first frame, never to future video

Actions

Action chunk of h = 32 as tokens in the action expert, denoised by flow matching; at inference the expert reads the single-pass video features through the shared attention

Prediction

Training: joint flow matching over actions and future video latents (paper: logit-normal t; released code: shift-warped uniform t with a bell-shaped loss weight); inference: one video-DiT pass over the clean first frame, then 10 action denoising steps at CFG 1.0 (no second pass)

Decoder

None at deployment: no future video tokens are instantiated, denoised or decoded

Memory

Single-chunk policy; the outer autoregressive loop is omitted. Within a chunk, the video DiT's per-layer K/V over the clean first-frame tokens is cached once and reused by all 10 action steps (Fig. 1C; code prefill_video_cache)

Speed

190 ms per chunk on one RTX 5090D V2 32 GB (authors); the imagine-then-execute variant Fast-WAM-IDM takes 810 ms on the same GPU

Key detail

Removing test-time imagination costs little accuracy while removing video co-training costs much; the deployed graph is 1 pass of the 5B DiT plus 10 passes of the 1B expert [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v2 Mar 2026). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2603.16666 Sec. 1, 3.2 and Fig. 1(C) (architecture, mask, KV cache, inference), 4.1 (Wan2.2-5B, d_a 1024, h 32, 10 steps, CFG 1.0, RTX 5090D), 4.3.3 (190 vs 810 ms); Hugging Face Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336); GitHub yuantianyuan01/FastWAM (MIT): configs/model/fastwam.yaml, configs/data/libero_2cam.yaml and robotwin.yaml, src/fastwam/models/wan22/mot.py, fastwam.py, schedulers/scheduler_continuous.py; Hugging Face yuanty/fastwam LIBERO and RoboTwin checkpoints.

comma.ai · 20262B DiT + 150M compressor

Block-causal driving DiT that trains openpilot

Driving & robotsclaim

Details
Overview

The learned driving simulator behind openpilot 0.11, whose driving policy comma calls the first robotics agent shipped to real users that was fully trained in a learned simulation. A ViT compressor turns the two camera views into a 32x16x32 latent, and a 2B block-causal diffusion transformer predicts the next frame latent, plus future actions, from 2 s of context, 6-DoF relative-pose actions and 1 s of future frames (so it is also an inverse dynamics model). Sampling is frame by frame with 15 Euler steps and CFG 2.0; with KV caching comma reports a sampling throughput of 12.2 frames/s per GPU (GPU and batch size not stated), not a latency.

Representation

ViT frame compressor (encoder 50M, decoder 100M, 2x deeper): two views (narrow, wide) of 3x128x256 → one 32x16x32 latent; DiT patch size and tokens per frame not stated (comma's later 4B world model uses 2x2 latent patches = 128 tokens per frame)

Core

2B diffusion transformer: 48 layers, d 1600, 25 heads (n_layer=48, n_head=25, n_embd=1600), 'adapted to 3 dimensional data'; norm, MLP and residual layout not disclosed, so the diagram draws only AdaLN-single and the attention layer; the post does not say what is written to the KV cache or when

Attention

Block-causal in every layer: tokens attend to their own frame and past frames; a sample = 2 s past context + 1 s future conditioning + 0-7 s simulation window at 5 fps (10 context frames [D])

Actions

6-DoF relative positions, diffusion noise level and frame indices injected via AdaLN-single (PixArt-α style)

Prediction

Rectified flow with logit-normal noise sampling; frame by frame, 15 Euler steps, classifier-free guidance 2.0 (up to 30 DiT passes per frame if the conditional and unconditional branches run separately [D]); noise-level augmentation for rollout robustness

Decoder

ViT decoder (100M) → narrow and wide 128x256 frames

Memory

KV cache enabled by the block-causal mask; context 2 s at 5 fps

Speed

12.2 frames/s per GPU throughput with KV caching (company claim; GPU type and batch size not stated); ≈366 DiT frame-evaluations per second per GPU at 15 steps × CFG [D]

Key detail

The on-policy driving model (a small transformer) is trained to predict the world model's suggested actions on rollouts generated with the world model and the latest policy checkpoint ('near on-policy'); the world model is trained on 2.5M minutes (≈41,700 h [D]) of driving video; weights release not stated on the page

Status and sources

blog post. Availability: closed. Sources: blog.comma.ai/011release (17 Mar 2026): sections Frame Compressor, Diffusion Transformer, sampling and throughput; arXiv 2504.19077 (Learning to Drive from a World Model, comma.ai), Sec. 4.2-4.3: RF objective, Euler step, latent rollout; PixArt-α (arXiv 2310.00426), Sec. 2.3: AdaLN-single; huggingface.co/commaai/worldmodel-4B README (later 4B model; patching and KV-cache comparison only).

page · SVG

NVIDIA · 202614B

One 14B DiT denoises video and actions together

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A 14B world-action model: the Wan2.1-I2V-14B image-to-video DiT is fully fine-tuned into a chunk-wise autoregressive flow-matching model that denoises the next 2 latent frames of video and the matching 1.6 s action chunk together, with one shared timestep and separate output decoders. Clean context sits in a KV cache (with the chunk being denoised, at most 4 chunks plus the first frame: 33 raw frames, 6.6 s), and after each chunk executes the predicted frames are replaced by encoded real observations. Naive inference costs 5.7 s per chunk; CFG on 2 GPUs, velocity caching (16 → 4 DiT steps), compilation, kernel and scheduler tuning, NVFP4 and the 1-step DreamZero-Flash schedule bring it to 150 ms on 2 GB200.

Representation

Frozen Wan2.1 VAE latents (480p model; 8x spatial, 4x temporal); 3 camera views resized to 176×320 and tiled 2×2 into one frame (code); 880 tokens per latent frame (DreamZero checkpoint config frame_seqlen); a full context of 33 raw frames encodes to 9 latent frames, the first frame plus 4 chunks of 2 [D: 33 = 1 + 4×8]

Core

Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P DiT with all blocks fine-tuned: 40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13,824 (base config.json); only state and action encoders plus an action decoder are added; text encoder, image encoder and VAE stay frozen; block internals not detailed in the paper (LayerNorm and RoPE named in its quantization notes)

Attention

Chunk-causal: the noisy current chunk (K = 2 latent frames + its action chunk) attends to the clean previous chunks; frames inside a chunk share one timestep; max context 8 latent frames (4 chunks) = 6.6 s

Actions

Action latents denoised jointly with the video in the same DiT, same timestep; chunks of 48 actions at 30 Hz (AgiBot) or 24 at 15 Hz (DROID) = 1.6 s; relative joint positions, Savitzky-Golay smoothed; the action encoder embeds the noisy actions with the timestep, the state encoder (2-layer MLP) adds one state token per chunk to the DiT sequence, and the action decoder (2-layer MLP) maps the action tokens to the action velocity at every step (code)

Prediction

Flow matching: 16 steps baseline → 4 effective with velocity caching (cached velocity reused when cosine similarity exceeds a threshold) → 1 step with DreamZero-Flash (video timesteps biased to high noise, t = 1 − Beta(7,1); action timesteps uniform)

Decoder

Wan2.1 VAE decoder turns predicted latents into future frames (Fig. 4 inference panel); not needed for control: actions come straight from the denoised action chunk, predicted video latents are discarded, and the released server decodes them only to save videos

Memory

KV cache refreshed with VAE-encoded real observations after every chunk (clean t = 0 pass; predicted frames discarded); it holds the first frame plus up to 3 earlier chunks (≤ 7 latent frames [D]), so with the chunk being denoised the window is 9 latent frames = 33 raw frames (code: local_attn_size = 4×2 + 1); cache reset every 4 chunks (code)

Speed

5.7 s per chunk naive on one GPU; with CFG split across 2 GPUs: 9.6x on H100 (~0.59 s [D]), 16.6x with NVFP4 (~350 ms at 4 steps) and 38x with Flash (150 ms at 1 step, ~7 Hz) on GB200 (company claims, Tables 1 and 3)

Key detail

Generating only actions gives a minimal speed-up at 14B (diffusion steps and DiT blocks dominate latency); the 38x comes from fewer DiT passes (16 → 4 by caching, → 1 with Flash), 2-GPU CFG, torch.compile + CUDA graphs, cuDNN attention + GPU-side scheduler, and NVFP4 (E2M1 weights and activations, FP8 QKV and softmax)

Overview

A real-time open world model: the high-noise expert of the middle-trained LingBot-World MoE (Wan2.2 I2V A14B architecture, two ≈14B experts, one active per timestep) is adapted to block-causal attention and distilled with DMD plus an adversarial head to 4 steps. By default it keeps the full KV cache of the whole rollout, so memory is emergent from context, but the cache grows by about 3.4 GB per 12-frame chunk and throughput falls from 8.9 to 3.6 FPS over a minute (WorldKV, 4×B200). The company claims 16 fps at 480p on one GPU node; the release script uses 8 GPUs.

Representation

Wan 3D causal VAE, stride 4x8x8 → 60x104 latent frame at 480x832; patch (1,2,2) → 1,560 tokens (30x52 grid) per latent frame [D]; chunk = 3 latent frames = 4,680 tokens = 12 output frames, 9 for the first chunk [D]

Core

Wan2.2 I2V A14B config: 40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13824; initialized from the high-noise expert of the middle-trained LingBot-World MoE (two ≈14B experts, one active per timestep), a dense causal DiT: 18.54B in the released checkpoint (14.29B Wan backbone + 4.26B camera layers; 14B in the paper)

Attention

Block-causal: bidirectional within a chunk, causal across chunks, KV cache; local_attn_size -1 and sink_size 0 by default = full KV over the whole rollout (window and sink exist as flags)

Actions

Released Fast: camera poses → per-pixel [ray origin, ray direction] → Plücker encoder (Linear 1536→5120 + residual MLP) → per-block MLP → scale and shift of the residual stream (no norm). The paper's rotation Plücker + multi-hot W/A/S/D keys is the Base (Act) variant; in Stage II only the action adapters were trained

Prediction

DMD with self-rollout plus an adversarial head on the fake-score network (APT-style, no R1/R2); 4 steps at indices [0, 179, 358, 679] of the 1,000-step schedule, shift 10 in the release CLI (generate() default 5); the bidirectional base samples 70 steps

Decoder

Wan VAE decoder at 480x832, 12 frames per chunk (9 for the first); the release decodes all chunks in one call after the rollout loop (README lists 480P & 720P)

Memory

No memory module: 'an emergent ability derived from the context window'; full KV ≈3.4 GB per 3-latent-frame chunk and >200 GB per minute (WorldKV; ≈3.8 GB per chunk by my count [D])

Speed

16 fps at 480p with <1 s latency on one GPU node (company claim; release script uses 8 GPUs with Ulysses sequence parallelism, GPU type not stated); WorldKV on 4×B200: 8.87 → 3.61 FPS over a one-minute rollout with full KV, WorldKV Table 1 at the last chunk of a rollout: 3.83 FPS vs 8.10 with a sliding window (4×H200: 2.36 vs 5.05)

Attention, not the GEMMs, sets the decay: after one minute each pass attends to ≈374k cached keys, ≈1.4 PFLOP of attention against ≈151 TFLOP of linear work per pass (≈112 Wan backbone + ≈39 camera adapters), ≈9.5x [D]

Robbyant · 20265.3B

Interleaves video and actions in one causal sequence

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A causal world-action model that interleaves video latents and actions in one autoregressive sequence with a KV cache. Two parallel transformer streams of the same depth, a 5B video stream initialised from Wan2.2-5B (d 3072) and a 0.35B action stream (d 768), are joined by shared attention. Each step denoises the next chunk (K = 4) with 3 Euler steps only to s = 0.6 (partial denoising, enabled by noisy-history augmentation), then decodes the chunk's actions (τK = 16 by the paper's formula) as inverse dynamics in 10 steps; real observations re-enter the cache in closed loop.

Representation

Wan2.2 causal VAE (4x16x16) plus 2x patchify; all camera views concatenated along the width → 192 spatial tokens per latent frame; video at 12.5 Hz with 4 actions per frame (50 Hz)

Core

MoT: video stream from Wan2.2-5B, 30 layers, d 3072 (24 heads, FFN 14,336 per the Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config); action stream of the same depth at d 768 (~350M), initialised by interpolating the video weights scaled by sqrt(d_v/d_a); RoPE in both; T5 text through cross-attention (which stream reads it is not stated); norms and timestep modulation not given in the paper

Attention

Causal over the interleaved video-action sequence (teacher forcing), bidirectional inside a chunk; action tokens are projected to d 3072 for the joint attention and back; training packs episodes into sequences of up to 10K tokens

Actions

Action tokens in the sequence (single-layer MLP encoder and decoder, hidden 256; quantile-normalised), decoded by inverse dynamics conditioned on the predicted visual transition; chunk K = 4 video frames = τK = 16 actions by the paper's formula [D]; released configs give 16-80 actions per chunk

Prediction

Flow matching with an Euler solver: video 3 steps to s = 0.6 (partial denoising) at CFG 5.0, actions 10 steps to s = 1.0 at CFG 1.0; a forward-dynamics step re-grounds the cache on the latest real frame

Decoder

Wan2.2 VAE decoder exists for visualisation, but actions are read from latents and the partially denoised video is never decoded for control

Memory

Causal KV cache over the interleaved history (released server: FIFO of the last 36 chunks for RoboTwin, 15 otherwise); the async-pipeline prose limits the active context to the last step, but Alg. 2 and Sec. 4.5.2 keep all cached history

Speed

Not disclosed: no latency, control rate or GPU is given; the authors name video-token denoising as the primary inference bottleneck

Key detail

Per chunk: 3 video steps x 2 CFG passes = 6 passes of the 5B stream over the new video tokens (768 if K = 4 latent frames of 192), plus 10 passes of the 0.35B stream, plus a cache-write pass over the encoded real frames and executed actions [D]

Status and sources

RSS 2026 (arXiv 2601.21998, v2 Mar 2026). Availability: code + weights (shared-backbone variant only). Sources: arXiv 2601.21998 Sec. 1, 3.2-3.4 (interleaving, MoT block, noisy-history augmentation, KV cache, async pipeline), Sec. 4.2 (dimensions, VAE, 192 tokens, sampling), Sec. 4 (12.5 Hz video / 50 Hz actions); Hugging Face Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336); github.com/robbyant/lingbot-va README, wan_va/configs/*.py, modules/model.py, wan_va_server.py; Project page technology.robbyant.com/lingbot-va (RSS 2026).

NVIDIA · 20262B

Video DiT predicts actions as extra latent frames

World-actionread

Details
Overview

Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World, a latent video diffusion transformer over Wan2.1 VAE latents, fully fine-tuned into a robot policy with no architectural change. Proprioception, the action chunk and the value are injected as extra latent frames: blank images are VAE-encoded and their latents overwritten with tiled copies of the vectors, so the denoising process that predicts future images also predicts actions. As a direct policy it denoises everything in parallel in 5 steps on LIBERO and RoboCasa (0.61 s per chunk on one H100; 10 steps and 0.95 s on ALOHA) and discards the future state and value; planning mode decodes them autoregressively for best-of-N search.

Representation

Wan2.1 VAE latent frames (8x spatial, 4x temporal, 16 channels); one latent frame per modality and camera view, e.g. 9 for LIBERO (blank, proprio, 2 views, action chunk, future proprio, 2 future views, value) or 11 with 3 cameras; each image is repeated 4x so one latent frame is one timestep; LIBERO data at 224 px per the repo config, i.e. ~196 tokens per latent frame with the 2x2 patch [D]

Core

Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World DiT, all weights fine-tuned: 28 blocks, d 2048, 16 heads, patch 2x2x1, 3D RoPE, AdaLN-LoRA timestep conditioning (repo net config COSMOS_V1_2B); T5 text via cross-attention; no new modules; Predict1 block design with QK RMSNorm

Attention

Bidirectional 3D self-attention over all latent frames; clean conditioning frames (current state) and noisy target frames share the sequence

Actions

The action chunk (K x d_act, scaled to [-1, 1], flattened and duplicated to fill H' x W' x C') overwrites a placeholder latent frame and is read back by averaging the copies; K = 16 (LIBERO, all executed), 32 (RoboCasa, 16 executed), 50 at 25 Hz (ALOHA)

Prediction

EDM denoising with sigma_max 80 and sigma_min 4: 5 steps (LIBERO, RoboCasa) or 10 (ALOHA) with action, future state and value in parallel, the latter two discarded; planning: autoregressive 10 + 5 + 5 steps, ensembles of 3 states and 5 values, best-of-N = 8

Decoder

Wan2.1 VAE decoder only to visualise predicted future images; actions and values are read from the latents without any decoding

Memory

None: the input is the current observation only, no history; 6.0-8.9 GB VRAM at inference without planning (README)

Speed

Per action chunk on one H100 (authors): 0.61 s at 5 steps, 0.95 s at 10, 0.16 s at 1 step (RoboCasa still 66.4% success at 1 step); best-of-8 planning 4.9 s on 8 parallel H100s

Key detail

Every step also denoises the future-state and value frames the policy throws away

Status and sources

ICLR 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2601.16163 Sec. 3 (base model, VAE), 4.1 (latent frame injection), 4.2 (parallel vs AR decoding), App. A.1 (injection details), A.2 (action chunks, training), A.3.1 and A.4.2 (steps, latency); GitHub NVlabs/cosmos-policy README (VRAM), net.py (COSMOS_V1_2B: 2048 channels, 28 blocks, 16 heads, patch 2, rope3d, adaln_lora 256), minimal_v4_dit.py (block order, AdaLN, no mask, patch embed per step) and cosmos_policy_experiment_configs.py (resolution 224, state_t 9).

Causal DiT with memory retrieved by camera view

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Tencent's real-time interactive world model: the HunyuanVideo-1.5 MM-DiT made chunk-wise block-causal (4 latent frames = 16 video frames per chunk) and distilled with Context Forcing to 4 steps. Each chunk attends to a memory rebuilt from the 3 most recent chunks, 1 chunk retrieved by field-of-view overlap and camera distance, and the first chunk kept as an attention sink, with RoPE indices re-assigned so old frames look recent. Keys enter through the timestep embedding, camera pose through a relative encoding inside attention. The company's 24 FPS at 720p needs 8 H800 GPUs with token parallelism, quantization and streaming VAE decode.

Representation

HunyuanVideo-1.5 causal 3D VAE: 16x spatial, 4x temporal, 32 channels; patch 1x1x1 → 3,600 tokens per latent frame at 720p, 14,400 per 4-latent chunk of 16 frames [D]

Core

HunyuanVideo-1.5 480P-I2V transformer: 54 double-stream MM-DiT blocks, d 2048, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4, GELU-tanh (HF config); no cross-attention in the released code: text tokens (2-layer token refiner) run in a parallel stream whose K/V join the video attention; timestep adaLN; 8B per the README (a 5B Wan-based variant is lighter but weaker)

Attention

Block-causal over chunks with a KV cache; context = 3 temporal + 1 spatial chunk + the first chunk as attention sink = 20 latents = 72,000 tokens at 720p (86,400 with the current chunk) [D]; temporal reframing re-assigns RoPE indices so context frames sit at a small relative distance

Actions

Dual representation: discrete keys → PE + zero-initialized MLP added to the timestep embedding (adaLN); camera pose → PRoPE relative encoding in a second attention term, output = Attn1 + zero_init(Attn2)

Prediction

Flow matching; Context Forcing distillation (memory-augmented bidirectional teacher, DMD loss) from 100 NFE to 4 denoising steps per 16-frame chunk

Decoder

HunyuanVideo-1.5 VAE decoder → 16 frames per chunk; progressive decode in small batches streamed over Triton, parallelized over 8 GPUs; the open checkpoints are 480P

Memory

Reconstituted context memory rebuilt per chunk by FOV-overlap and camera-distance retrieval from past chunks; no explicit 3D state; its KV cache is recomputed in one extra pass per chunk; KV ≈63.7 GB in BF16 for the 72,000-token context (RoPE and PRoPE K/V both cached), ≈8.0 GB per GPU when split 8 ways [D]

Speed

24 FPS at 720p on 8×H800 (company claim); Table 4: 2.80 → 3.80 (DiT parallelism + quantization) → 16.0 (+VAE) → 24.0 FPS (+streaming decode); 4.95 FPS for the 8B model on 4×H200 (measured by WorldKV); 28 GB per GPU at sp=8 (README)

Key detail

Distillation cuts passes 25x, but the remaining 8.57x to real time is systems work; ≈90% of per-chunk DiT FLOPs is attention: two attention terms (RoPE and PRoPE) per block over ≈86,400 tokens [D]

NVIDIA's physical-AI world foundation model: a flow-matching DiT that generates a whole 93-frame clip (24 latent frames, 5.8 s at 16 fps) with full self-attention, unifying Text2World, Image2World and Video2World by replacing conditioning frames in the sequence and flagging them with a mask token. Full (bidirectional) self-attention over all tokens of the clip; training at 720p/93 frames uses context parallelism 2 (2B) or 8 (14B) (Table 9)

Wan2.1 VAE decoder → 93 frames at up to 1280x704

Few-step space-time transformer with agent heads

Causal DiTverified

Details
Overview

A scalable world model that trains a Minecraft agent entirely offline inside its own imagination. A 400M block-causal transformer tokenizer (masked autoencoding, continuous tanh bottleneck) turns each 360x640 frame into 512 latent tokens of 16 channels, which the dynamics model reshapes into 256 spatial tokens of 32 channels. A 1.6B block-causal dynamics transformer, factorized over space and time with temporal attention in every 4th layer and GQA, denoises the next frame's tokens with a shortcut-forcing objective in K = 4 passes. The context is 192 frames (9.6 s), the model runs at 21 FPS on one H100, and policy, reward and value heads read agent tokens inside the same transformer.

Representation

256 spatial tokens x 32 channels per frame (a 512x16 bottleneck reshaped) from a 400M block-causal MAE tokenizer with a continuous tanh bottleneck; 384x640 padded input = 960 patches of 16x16

Core

1.6B dynamics transformer: pre-RMSNorm, RoPE (layers and axes not given), SwiGLU, QKNorm, attention logit soft-capping; layer, head and width counts not disclosed in the paper; repeat unit of 3 space layers + 1 causal time layer (Fig. 2b); each layer is drawn as a pre-norm residual block with a SwiGLU MLP, as the paper starts from 'a standard transformer with pre-layer RMSNorm, RoPE, and SwiGLU' and names 'the FLOPs of the MLPs'

Attention

Block-causal: all tokens of a frame attend to each other and to the past; space-only and time-only layers, temporal attention every 4th layer, GQA; context 192 frames = 49,152 spatial tokens [D]

Actions

Interleaved tokens: each action component (mouse, keyboard) is encoded into S_a tokens and summed with a learned embedding; each frame block also carries S_r registers and one shortcut signal-level/step-size token

Prediction

Shortcut forcing (diffusion forcing + shortcut models, x-prediction, ramp loss weight): K = 4 passes per frame instead of 64, no separate distillation; rollouts stay in latent space, and context latents, generated ones included, are re-noised to tau_ctx = 0.1

Decoder

The tokenizer's block-causal transformer decoder, frame by frame, to 360x640

Memory

KV cache over 192 frames (9.6 s); size not computable from the disclosed numbers; the authors name MLP FLOPs and KV-cache bandwidth as the inference limits

Speed

21 FPS at 640x360 on one H100 (authors, Table 1); the design cascade runs 0.8 → 9.1 (4-step shortcut) → 18.9 (temporal attention every 4 layers) → 23.2 (GQA) → … → 21.4 FPS at 256 tokens (Table 2)

Key detail

Agent tokens attend to everything but nothing attends back to them, so policy, reward and value heads share the world model's trunk and read the agent-token outputs; the transformer stays frozen during imagination training

arXiv preprint. Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2509.24527 Sec. 3.1-3.4, Sec. 4, App. A, Fig. 2, Tables 1-2; danijar.com/project/dreamer4 (official page; no code released); Shazeer 2020, GLU variants (SwiGLU, ref. [34]).

Details
Overview

A 32B dense decoder-only LLM mid-trained on observation-action trajectories: Python execution traces (stack-frame locals after each executed line) and agentic Docker sessions. The same transformer is policy and world model; a world-model step is ordinary text generation of the next observation. For compute it is plain long-context LLM decoding, kept affordable by GQA and a 3:1 local/global pattern (47 layers with an 8k window, 17 with 131k) that allows a KV cache of about 10 GiB per 131k-token sequence when the local layers keep only their window [D].

Representation

Text and code tokens, Llama 3 BPE tokenizer, vocabulary 128,256; an observation is the stack-frame locals as JSON, an action is the Python line executed (custom separator tokens)

Core

Dense decoder-only: 64 layers, d 6144, FFN 21,504 (SwiGLU), 48 query heads of 128, 8 KV heads (GQA), RMSNorm pre-norm; 32B parameters

Attention

Document-causal; local sliding window 8,192 tokens and global window 131,072 tokens interleaved 3:1, with the last layer also global: 47 local + 17 global layers (global at 0, 4, …, 60 and 63; Fig. 6a, config); scaled RoPE in every layer, θ 1M, scale factor 16

Actions

Actions are text in the stream (a Python statement or an agent tool call); the next observation is generated as text after it

Prediction

Next-token softmax over 128k vocabulary; one pass per token, so one trace step costs as many passes as its frame has tokens (locals JSON, separators and the source line)

Decoder

None; the output is text (trace frames, code, tool calls)

Memory

KV cache per token per layer 4 KiB in bf16 (K and V, 8 KV heads × 128); at 131k context 8.5 GiB for the 17 global layers + 1.47 GiB for the 47 local layers (8k window) ≈ 10 GiB, vs 32 GiB if every layer kept the full context [D]; the released FastGen engine (paged attention, host-side KV cache) keeps full-length KV in all 64 layers, 256 KiB per token [D]

Speed

No decode-throughput figure; inference fits one 80 GB H100 with quantization (authors; bf16 weights alone are 65 GB [D]); trained on 2,048 H100s for pre- and mid-training (Table 3)

13T pre- and mid-training tokens, the last 5T in the code-world-model mid-training stage at 131k context (trace and agent data are 30% of that mix); the world model is the LLM itself, so running it is long-context LLM decoding

Slow-fast asynchronous inference: 1 flow-matching step of the video DiT with its latents cached, then 5 action denoising steps on that cache; video DiT at 5 Hz vs action model at 30 Hz (1:6)

Frozen video VAE decoder, used when GE-Base / GE-Sim generate video; GE-Act deployment skips video decoding (return_video=False), though the paper also shows GE-Act generating videos

Sparse memory: 4 conditioning frames per view (code: 3 sampled earlier frames plus the current one), each one latent frame; the paper's GE-Base text counts the initial frame separately

54-step trajectory in 200 ms on an onboard RTX 4090 mounted on the robot (authors), i.e. 5 chunks/s [D]; training: GE-Base-MR 32 A100 x ~7 days, GE-Base-LF 32 A100 x ~3 days, GE-Act pretraining 16 A100 x ~3 days

Details
Overview

A single autoregressive transformer, initialised from Chameleon, that treats images, text and actions as one token vocabulary: it predicts the next frame's VQ-GAN codes as a world model and the next action's 7 tokens as a VLA, and the authors report that training both together helps both. Representation

VQ-GAN image tokenizer (compression 16, codebook 8192): 256 tokens per 256x256 frame or 1,024 per 512x512; BPE text; one shared vocabulary of 65,536 including the 8192 image and 256 action tokens

Core

Chameleon-initialised decoder-only LLM; the paper gives no size, the released base_model config.json has 32 layers, d 4096, 32 heads, FFN 11,008 (~7B; 14 GB of bf16 safetensors [D]); block details not disclosed in the paper

Attention

Causal over text, image and action tokens in world-model mode; in action mode a mask lets each action attend to text and images but not to earlier actions of the chunk; default M = 2 input frames

Actions

7 discrete tokens per action (3 relative positions, 3 relative angles, 1 gripper), 256 bins per dimension; chunks of K = 5 (K = 10 on LIBERO-Long)

Prediction

Next-token softmax, greedy in the released code; 9 passes per action ([BOA], 7 tokens, [EOA]) [D]; the masked chunk can be generated in parallel (authors); about 277 or 1,061 serial passes per generated frame (256 / 1,024 VQ codes plus row-end, size, [BOI], [EOI] and end tokens) [D]

Decoder

VQ-GAN decoder for predicted image tokens (world-model mode); actions need only a de-binning lookup (token → bin centre → min-max un-normalisation), no neural decoder

Memory

LLM KV cache over the prompt (history frames + text); 1, 2 or 4 history frames evaluated, 2 by default

Speed

LIBERO, GPU not stated (authors, Table 5): 2.27 / 1.77 / 1.22 FPS with 1 / 2 / 4 history frames without chunking, 3.67 / 3.13 / 2.78 FPS with chunking

Key detail

An LLM-style decode workload, token-serial; each imagined frame is about 277 (256×256) to 1,061 (512×512) decode steps [D]; 'memory-bandwidth-bound' is our estimate for batch-1 decode of a 7B model, not an author measurement

HunyuanVideo 3D VAE decoder → 33-frame chunk at 720p, 25 fps

Details
Overview

Autoregressive Adversarial Post-Training, the one-pass-per-frame design: a pre-trained 8B video diffusion transformer is made block-causal and post-trained adversarially so that each latent frame (4 video frames) is generated with a single network evaluation from noise, the previous generated frame recycled through channel concatenation, and a KV cache over a sliding window of 30 latent frames. Per-frame conditions (human pose, or camera rays relative to the previous frame) enter as extra input channels. The authors report 24 fps at 736x416 on one H100 with 0.16 s latency, or 1280x720 on 8 H100s, for streams up to a minute.

Representation

Causal 3D convolution VAE, 4x temporal and 8x spatial; one latent frame = 4 video frames, the first frame its own latent; DiT patch size not stated, so tokens per frame are not computed (latent grid 92x52 at 736x416 [D])

Core

8B MMDiT-style diffusion transformer with 36 blocks (base model not named); width and heads not stated; text tokens and visual tokens in one sequence; the discriminator reuses the same causal architecture (generator + discriminator = 16B in training); norm, FFN and residual layout not stated, so the diagram draws only the attention layer

Attention

Block-causal: text tokens attend only to themselves, visual tokens to the text tokens and to visual tokens of the current and previous frames; window N = 30 latent frames (5 s; N = 15 at 1280x720) plus the text tokens and the first frame always; FlashAttention-3; 3D RoPE with a fixed temporal interval for arbitrary length

Actions

Each step channel-concatenates noise k, condition k and the previous generated latent frame (the encoded user frame at step 1); camera: ray origin and direction relative to the previous frame (modified CameraCtrl II) as new input channels with a randomly initialized input projection; pose: per-frame condition following OmniHuman-1; the discriminator shifts the conditions to align with its frame inputs

Prediction

1 NFE per latent frame: diffusion adaptation, consistency-distillation initialization, then adversarial training with student forcing (the generator rolls out with its KV cache during training; frame-wise discriminator logits, approximated R1/R2); one frame of computation per AR step vs two for one-step diffusion forcing (Sec. 2.1, Fig. 2)

Decoder

Lightweight VAE decoder: residual blocks per scale 3 → 2, channels [128, 256, 512, 512] → [64, 128, 256, 512], ≈3x faster; causal VAE allows streaming decode of 4 frames per step

Memory

Sliding window of 30 latent frames in the KV cache (constant speed and memory); the effective receptive field still grows across layers and steps, which is why training uses long student-forced rollouts

Speed

24 fps at 736x416 on one H100, 1280x720 on 8×H100, 0.16 s latency (0.17 s at 1280x720), 60 s streams of 1,440 frames (authors); 6 DiT passes per second, so ≤167 ms per latent-frame pass including decode [D]; trained on 256 H100s with 8-GPU Ulysses context parallelism

Key detail

One frame of DiT compute per AR step: the previous latent rides along as input channels, so no clean frame is computed again (one-step diffusion forcing computes two frames per step; Sec. 2.1, Fig. 2); each pass yields one latent frame = 4 video frames; no code or weights (authors: proprietary, not scheduled for release)

Frame-local attention: bidirectional within a 5-frame chunk, causal to the previous chunk, effective window k = 10 frames (FlexAttention). The SSM scans over time independently per spatial block (b_h, b_w), block sizes differing by layer to trade spatial coherence for temporal memory

Continuous actions (camera position) through a small MLP added to the noise-level embedding, injected by adaptive normalisation; discrete Minecraft actions as learned embeddings

University of Washington, TRI · 2025≈385M + ResNet-18

Two timesteps turn one DiT into policy or dynamics

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A diffusion transformer that couples an action diffusion process and a future-image diffusion process with two independent timesteps. Fixing a timestep at T marginalises that modality and fixing it at 0 conditions on it, so one network is a policy, a forward model, an inverse model or a video predictor. The current frames condition every block through AdaLN (ResNet-18 features), while the future frames are SDXL-VAE latents patchified into tokens next to 16 action tokens and 8 registers.

Representation

Future observation: 224x224 frames → frozen SDXL VAE → 28x28x4 latents, patchified (4,4,2) → 49 tokens per camera per 2-frame stack [D]; current observation (h_o = 2 frames per camera) → trainable ImageNet-initialised ResNet-18 features, used only as AdaLN conditioning

Core

DiT with AdaLN: depth 12, d 768, 12 heads, MLP ratio 4, 8 register tokens; ≈368M in the 12 blocks [D] (85.0M attention + MLP, 283.2M AdaLN modulation from a 5120-d condition), ≈385M for the whole denoiser [D] (DROID config, 3 cameras); trained from scratch, no base video model; MLP Linear → GELU → Linear (code)

Attention

Bidirectional over action tokens + future-image patches + registers; for the 3-camera DROID setup 16 + 3 x 49 + 8 = 171 tokens [D]; learnable positional embedding

Actions

16-step action chunk, one token per step through a shallow shared MLP; AdaLN carries the two timestep embeddings (action, image) and the ResNet features; 8 actions executed before replanning

Prediction

DDPM training with 100 steps, DDIM sampling with 10; policy mode fixes the image timestep at T (paper; the released code uses the first DDIM timestep, 90 of 0-99), so the image tokens are pure noise but stay in the sequence

Decoder

SDXL VAE decoder, only when images are sampled (forward dynamics, video); the policy never decodes

Memory

None beyond the 2-frame observation stack

Speed

Inference latency not disclosed; the robot runs at 10 Hz with delta end-effector actions; DROID pretraining of 100K steps takes 24 h on 4 A100 (authors)

Key detail

Per chunk 10 passes of the 12-block stack (≈368M parameters, ≈85M of them applied per token) over 171 tokens ≈ 0.3 TFLOP [D]; about 36x fewer parameters than DreamZero's 14B [D]

Status and sources

RSS 2025. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2504.02792 Sec. III-B/C (coupled timesteps, architecture, registers), App. A (implementation, DDIM, 24 h on 4 A100), App. C (10 Hz control), Table V (hyperparameters); github.com/WEIRDLabUW/unified-world-model: configs/model/uwm.yaml, configs/dataset/droid.yaml, models/uwm/uwm.py, models/uwm/obs_encoder.py, models/common/adaln_attention.py, models/common/attention.py, README (released checkpoints).

Details
Overview

An open-source (code; weights taken down), real-time Minecraft world model: a LLaMA-style decoder trained on interleaved frame and action tokens. A VQ-VAE with 16x spatial compression turns each 224x384 frame into 336 tokens (14x24, codebook 8,192); a separate action tokenizer turns each action into 11 tokens. Diagonal decoding generates tokens along diagonals in parallel, and a fine-tune with a matching attention mask narrows the quality gap; the 1.2B model goes from 0.89 to 3.01 FPS.

Representation

336 discrete tokens per 224x384 frame (14x24 from a VQ-VAE with 16x spatial compression, codebook 8,192); frames downscaled from 360x640 'to reduce the computation'

Core

LLaMA architecture (pre-norm RMSNorm, RoPE theta 10,000; code: SwiGLU FFN, GQA with 4 KV heads, head dim 64, no biases): 1.2B = 20 layers, d 2048, MLP 8192, 32 heads; 700M = 20 layers, d 2048, MLP 4096, 32 heads; 300M = 20 layers, d 1024, MLP 4096, 16 heads

Attention

Dense causal over 16-frame clips: 16 x 347 = 5,552 tokens [D]; vocabulary 8,192 + 70 = 8,262

Actions

11 action tokens per step ([aBOS], 9 action tokens incl. 2 camera tokens, [aEOS]) interleaved after each frame; the model predicts actions too, so it doubles as a policy

Prediction

Next-token AR, or diagonal decoding: tokens (i, j+1) and (i+1, j) are released together, 37 passes per frame instead of 336 at k = 1 (theoretical 9.1x) [D]; the released code defaults to k = 2 (50 passes, 6.7x) [D], and the k behind Table 2 is not stated; fine-tuned with a matching parallel attention mask

Decoder

VQ-VAE decoder → 224x384 frame

Memory

Static full KV cache over the 16-frame, 5,552-position context (4 KV heads; about 114 MB fp16 for 1.2B [D]); no rolling window: when full, the demo keeps the last 8 frames, clears the cache and re-prefills. 32-frame configs (11,104 positions) exist for 700M and 1.2B

Speed

1.2B: 0.89 FPS autoregressive, 3.01 FPS with diagonal decoding; 300M: 2.00 / 5.91 FPS (authors, Table 2; inference GPU not stated). Trained on 32 A100-40GB for 200k steps

Key detail

Diagonal decoding cuts passes per frame 9.1x at k = 1 (6.7x at the code's default k = 2), yet FPS rises only 3.4x for 1.2B [D]; the sources do not analyse the gap. The authors' real-time bar is 2 FPS for amateurs and 5 FPS for professionals

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: code (MIT); weights taken down May 2025. Sources: arXiv 2504.08388 Sec. 2.1-2.3 (tokenizer, decoder, diagonal decoding), Sec. 3.1-3.2 (data, training), Tables 1-2, App. B Table 6; github.com/microsoft/MineWorld: README (news), LICENSE, configs/*.yaml, lvm.py, mineworld.py, inference.py, diagonal_decoding.py.

University of Würzburg · 2025≈9.5M transformer

DreamerV3 with a transformer and contrastive loss

RL world modelverified

Details
Overview

DreamerV3 with its GRU replaced by a small Transformer State-Space Model and an extra action-conditioned contrastive objective. A CNN VAE encodes 64x64 frames as 32x32 categoricals, an action mixer fuses state and action into one token, and a 4-block causal transformer with Transformer-XL relative positions predicts the next state, reward and continuation. The cache is capped at 8 steps, so per-step memory is bounded. Swapping in the transformer alone scores like DreamerV3; the gain comes from AC-CPC, which predicts features 10 steps ahead given the future actions and helps the transformer far more than DreamerV3's RSSM (mean HNS 162 vs 121).

Representation

32 categoricals x 32 classes per 64x64 RGB frame from a CNN VAE (4 strided conv layers)

Core

TSSM: 4 blocks, d 512, 8 heads, FFN 1024, dropout 0.1; ≈9.5M transformer parameters [D] (≈10.8M with the action mixer and dynamics head)

Attention

Causal self-attention with Transformer-XL relative positions; attention context 8 steps; training sequences T = 64, batch 16

Actions

Action mixer (Linear + LN + SiLU, then Linear + LN, both to 512) fuses the flattened 32x32 state with the one-hot action into one token

Prediction

One pass per imagined step; a linear dynamics head (512 → 32x32 logits) samples the next categorical state from h_t; imagination horizon 15

Decoder

CNN decoder reconstructs from z_t for training only; the actor-critic uses s_t = {h_t, z_t}, so nothing is decoded in imagination

Memory

Hidden states of the previous segment are cached and reused as context; the released code caps the cache at 8 steps (att_context_left = 8)

Speed

No inference or wall-clock figure in the paper; Atari 100k mean/median HNS 162/77 (authors)

Key detail

AC-CPC: InfoNCE prediction of latent features K = 10 steps (~0.67 s) ahead, conditioned on future actions; without the action conditioning HNS drops from 162/77 to 111/42

Status and sources

ICLR 2025. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2503.04416 Sec. 3.1-3.2, 4.3 (Table 3); App. A Tables 4, 6-9; github.com/burchim/TWISTER nnet/models/twister.py (att_context_left = 8), nnet/modules/twister/tssm.py.

Wayve · 20258.4B + 285M tokenizer

Factorized-attention DiT over five cameras

Driving & robotsread

Details
Overview

Wayve's multi-camera driving world model: a video tokenizer with 32x spatial and 8x temporal compression turns up to 5 camera streams into 64-channel latents, and an 8.4B space-time factorized transformer denoises them with flow matching. The ego action and flow-matching time enter through adaptive LayerNorm; 3D agent boxes, scene and road-layout metadata and CLIP or scenario embeddings through cross-attention; camera geometry and timestamps as added encodings. It runs 50 denoising steps; Wayve describes no KV cache, reports no inference speed and lists distillation and faster, near-real-time synthesis as future work.

Representation

Video tokenizer (space-time factorized transformer, 85M encoder / 200M decoder): 8x temporal, 32x spatial, 64 channels; 24 frames at 448x960 → 3x14x30 latents (≈400x compression); 420 latents per camera per latent step, 2,100 across 5 cameras [D]

Core

22 space-time factorized transformer blocks, d 4096, 32 heads, 8.4B parameters; each block adds the position, timestamp and camera encodings, then runs spatial attention (over space and cameras), temporal attention, cross-attention and an MLP with adaptive LayerNorm; QK-norm before each attention. Not described, so not drawn: where else adaptive LayerNorm sits, and the residual connections

Attention

Factorized: spatial attention over 2,100 tokens (5 cameras × 420) [D], temporal attention over 6 latent steps; training window 48 frames × 5 cameras = 12,600 tokens; no full 3D attention; sinusoidal space and timestamp encodings plus learned camera geometry, re-added at the start of every block

Actions

Ego-vehicle action (speed, curvature) and flow-matching time via adaptive LayerNorm in every block (found more accurate than cross-attention); 3D agent boxes, metadata (incl. road layout) and CLIP or scenario embeddings via cross-attention; camera geometry and timestamps are added to the latents with the positional encodings

Prediction

Flow matching, 50 denoising steps, linear-quadratic schedule, no distillation; CFG off by default (scale 2-20 for hard cases); rollout in latent space: k=3 context latents, predict the next set of latents (3 per stride in Fig. 2), append, slide the window

Decoder

200M decoder with 24 space-time factorized blocks (16 + 8, d 512, 16 heads): jointly decodes 3 latent steps into 24 frames at 448x960 per camera; sliding window at inference

Memory

Sliding window of latents; no KV cache described

Speed

Not disclosed; 'real-time or near-real-time video synthesis remains computationally intensive', distillation listed as future work (authors); ≈1.1e16 dense FLOPs per 50-step, 48-frame, 5-camera window [D]

Key detail

Wayve chose 32x spatial / 64-channel latents because shorter latent sequences give faster inference and better memory efficiency, and the model captures dynamics better; ≈1.5e12 training tokens on 256 H100s [D]

Status and sources

company technical report (arXiv 2503.20523). Availability: closed. Sources: GAIA-2 technical report, arXiv 2503.20523v1: Sec. 2.1 tokenizer (85M/200M, 8x/32x, 64 ch), 2.2 world model (22 blocks, C=4096, 32 heads, conditioning), 4 training (12,600 tokens, 256 H100), 5 inference (50 steps, k=3, CFG), 8 future work; Fig. 2, Fig. 3; Wayve GAIA-2 page, https://wayve.ai/thinking/gaia-2/.

World and Human Action Model: a nanoGPT-style causal transformer trained from scratch on seven years of Bleeding Edge gameplay to predict interleaved image and controller-action tokens. 540 discrete tokens per 300x180 frame from a ~300M ViT-VQGAN, vocabulary 16,384 (1.6B model); the 15M-894M models use 256 tokens per 128x128 frame from a ~60M conv VQGAN, vocabulary 4,096

Core

Modified nanoGPT implementation of GPT-2, 1.6B parameters (also 15M-894M); 24 layers, 18 heads, width 2304, FFN 9216 (released code)

Attention

Dense causal over 5,560 tokens = 1 s = 10 frames at 10 Hz (2,720 tokens for the 894M model)

Actions

Xbox controller as 16 tokens per step [D: (5,560 - 10 x 540) / 10]: 12 buttons plus the x and y of both sticks discretized into 11 buckets; no delimiter token, the learned positions tell the modalities apart; actions are predicted as well as consumed

Prediction

Next-token softmax: at least 540 serial passes per frame plus the 16 action tokens [D]

Decoder

ViT-VQGAN decoder → 300x180 frame

Released code: KV cache within a step (prefill the window, then one cached pass per token), rebuilt for each modality (image, then action); 1 s window of 10 steps slides, positions restart at 0

About 1 fps for WHAM-1.6B against 10+ fps for the MaskGIT-based WHAMM (Microsoft Research WHAMM article, 4 Apr 2025; the Nature paper gives no inference figure). Training: 200k updates x 2.5M tokens = 5e11 tokens [D]; 98 H100s, 5 days (HF model card)

556 sequential tokens per frame at 1.6B with a 5,560-token context: per-frame decode like GAIA-1 (576 image tokens, 6.5B) at a quarter of its size and about a third of its 15,860-token context [D]; the fix was MaskGIT decoding (WHAMM)

Stanford · 20250.5B

Video and action heads on one masked transformer

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A masked-autoencoder-style transformer, initialised from MAR-B, that fuses a history of kl-f16 VAE latents and action chunks into a joint video-action latent, which two lightweight diffusion heads decode into video patches and actions. Denoising runs only in the small heads, never in the backbone, and at deployment the video head is skipped entirely, so a 16-action trajectory costs 95 ms on an RTX 3080: 40 ms of VAE encoding, 40 ms of transformer (30 with flash attention) and 15 ms for 16 steps of the action head.

Representation

Pretrained kl-f16 VAE latent map (w x h x c) per frame, flattened and projected by an FC layer into N tokens of width d; official config: 256×256 frames, 16×16×16 latents, so N = 256 tokens per frame and h = 4 frames (the paper gives neither); future frames enter as randomly masked tokens concatenated channel-wise with the history tokens

Core

MAE-style transformer initialised from MAR-B and itself mar_base (official code: 12 encoder + 12 decoder timm ViT blocks, pre-LN, d 768, 12 heads, MLP ratio 4); 0.5B parameters in total (paper, no breakdown); language (Libero10, UMI multi-task) is a CLIP ViT-B/32 text token projected 512 → 768, repeated M times (64 in code) and concatenated into the token sequence; the paper calls this cross-attention, but the code has no cross-attention layer

Attention

Bidirectional (no attention mask in code) over the N x h video-action tokens + M language tokens; the same positions are masked in every frame to avoid leakage; the paper says attention takes half of the inference time; Table VI: transformer 40 of 95 ms, 30 with flash attention

Actions

Each frame pairs with a chunk of L actions sampled faster than frames; history chunks are repeated M times, FC-projected to N action tokens and concatenated channel-wise with the visual tokens

Prediction

Video: MAR-style masked generation from an empty sequence in 1 to 8 autoregressive stages; actions: a conv + MLP pool the N latents into one action latent that conditions the action diffusion head, 16 denoising steps on the robot (100 in simulation)

Decoder

Video diffusion head + VAE decoder exist but are skipped at deployment (100 ms at 16 steps, 625 ms at 100)

Memory

History window of h frames and action chunks; no KV cache

Speed

Per 16-action trajectory on an RTX 3080 (authors, Table VI): VAE encoder 40 ms, transformer 40 ms (30 with flash attention), action head 15 ms at 16 steps (93 at 100); total 95 ms (85 with flash attention), 173 ms at 100 steps; policy + planner 195 ms; simulation timings on L40

Key detail

Trained with video, deployed without it: the skipped video head (100 ms) would cost more than the whole 95 ms policy, and the VAE encoder plus backbone, not the action head, dominate (80 of 95 ms [D])

Status and sources

RSS 2025 (arXiv v3, 24 Apr 2025). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2503.00200 Sec. III-A/B/C (encoding, masked transformer, diffusion heads), V-D (0.5B, 16 vs 100 steps, attention share), App. X-A (autoregressive video stages), X-D and Table VI (timing); Official code: model/autoregressive/mar_con_unified.py (mar_base 12 + 12 blocks, CLIP text tokens concatenated), config/model/uva.yaml (256x256, vae_stride 16, 4 frames), timm 0.9.7 ViT Block; GitHub README (MAR + VAE initialisation, checkpoints, 8 H100 x 4 days); LTH14/mar models/mar.py; Project page (RSS 2025).

Next-token softmax, 2,560 passes per latent frame [D]; Medusa speculative decoding (single-layer FFN heads on the last hidden state that share the output layer, no tree attention; tested on 4B/5B; the released code has no Medusa model): the chosen 9 heads give 2.0x token throughput and 4.2x fewer passes for 4B, 3.2x and 5.7x for 5B [D]; 12 heads give the fewest passes (4.6x, 6.1x) (Table 15, 8 H100)

Meta FAIR · 20241B

Navigation DiT that cross-attends to past frames

Driving & robotsread

Details
Overview

A navigation world model for robots that predicts the next egocentric frame latent from past frames and a 3-DoF navigation action. Its Conditional Diffusion Transformer runs self-attention only over the tokens of the frame being denoised and reads the 4 context frames through cross-attention, so cost is linear in the context length (about 4x fewer FLOPs than a DiT over all frames). Planning is model-predictive control with the cross-entropy method, or ranking 32 trajectories from an external policy. The default 250 denoising steps make a 4 s trajectory cost 30.3 s on an RTX 6000 Ada; distillation to 6 steps and time skipping bring it to 0.4 s (authors).

Representation

Stable Diffusion VAE (sd-vae-ft-ema) latents of 224×224 frames (4:3 centre crop, then resize): 4×28×28 latent, 2×2 patches → 196 tokens per frame (code) [D]; rollouts at 4 FPS

Core

CDiT-XL, 1B parameters (sizes S to XL); XL/2 = 28 blocks, width 1152, 16 heads, patch 2, MLP ratio 4, the DiT-XL/2 shape (code); block = self-attention over the target frame, cross-attention to context frames with a skip connection, MLP; AdaLN scale, shift and gates

Attention

Self-attention within the target frame only (n tokens); cross-attention from target queries to the tokens of m = 4 context frames as keys and values; cost O(m n² d) vs O(m² n² d) for a full DiT; CDiT-L is 4x faster than DiT-XL at equal parameters with better prediction

Actions

Navigation action a = (u ∈ R² translation, yaw φ): each scalar → sine-cosine features → 2-layer MLP to d/3 dims, concatenated into ψ_a; time shift k (up to ±16 s) and diffusion timestep t each embedded to R^d the same way; ξ = ψ_a + ψ_k + ψ_t drives AdaLN; actions omitted for unlabeled Ego4D training

Prediction

DDPM with the DiT noise schedule and learned covariance (VLB loss); 250 denoising steps by default, distilled to 6 (FastVideo DiT distillation); 'Time Skip' composes adjacent action pairs to simulate 8 instead of 16 states for 4 s

Decoder

SD VAE decoder → pixels, used for LPIPS goal scoring during planning and for visualization

Memory

4 context frames re-encoded as cross-attention keys and values at every step; no KV cache discussed; loses context on out-of-distribution data (mode collapse noted by the authors)

Speed

One 4 s trajectory (16 states) on one RTX 6000 Ada: 30.3 s default → 14.7 s with Time Skip (8 states) → 0.4 s with 6-step distillation → 0.1 s with 4-bit quantization (estimated, not measured) (authors, Table 8); ≈7.4-8.3 ms per pass in the three measured configurations, ≈2.1 ms implied by the 4-bit estimate [D]; trained on 64 H100s (8 machines × 8 GPUs)

Key detail

All of the ≈76x speedup comes from fewer passes (4,000 → 48: 250 → 6 steps, 16 → 8 states), none from cheaper passes; ranking 32 trajectories costs 32 × 8 × 6 = 1,536 passes per decision, run as 48 sequential batch-32 passes [D]

Status and sources

CVPR 2025. Availability: code + weights. Sources: NWM paper, arXiv 2412.03572: Sec. 3.1-3.3 (CDiT block, action encoding, AdaLN, complexity), 4.1 (implementation: CDiT-XL 1B, 4 context frames, SD VAE, 64 H100), Fig. 2, App. 8.2 and Table 8 (runtime); Official code github.com/facebookresearch/nwm: models.py (CDiT, XL/2 config), misc.py (224 crop), config/wm_debug_bs_32.yaml, diffusion/ (DDPM sampler).

Details
Overview

A task-agnostic latent world model that predicts future DINOv2 patch features instead of pixels. A frozen DINOv2 turns each 196x196 frame into 196 patch features of width 384, and a small ViT predictor (6 layers, ~19M parameters) regresses the next frame's features from a history of up to 3 frames, with the action and proprioception embeddings concatenated onto every patch vector rather than added as tokens. Goals are images; planning is cross-entropy-method search in feature space, and the pixel decoder exists only for visualization.

Representation

196 patch features (14x14 x 384) per frame resized to 196x196, from a frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (dinov2_vits14 in the official config; the paper does not name the variant)

Core

ViT with the patch-embedding layer removed, used as a decoder-only predictor: depth 6, 16 heads, MLP 2048, ~19M parameters (paper; the predictors in the released checkpoints have 20.1M at H = 3 and 19.96M at H = 1 [D]); token width 404 = 384 features + 10-d action + 10-d proprio (official code); the code also uses pre-LayerNorm blocks, GELU in the MLP, a learned absolute position embedding per (frame, patch) slot added once at the input, and a final LayerNorm, none of which the paper describes

Attention

Frame-level causal mask: every patch of frame t attends to all patches of frames t-H..t-1 (no token-level autoregression); H = 3 (PointMaze, Reacher, Push-T, PushObj) or 1 (Wall, Rope, Granular); at most 3 x 196 = 588 tokens [D]

Actions

A linear layer (a 1x1 Conv1d in the official code and weights; the paper calls it an MLP) maps the frameskip-stacked action to a 10-d embedding that is concatenated to every patch vector (channels, not tokens); proprioception enters the same way through its own 10-d linear layer; frameskip 5 (1 for Rope and Granular)

Prediction

One pass regresses the next frame's 196 features (MSE in latent space); no sampling, no pixels

Decoder

Optional transposed-convolution decoder trained separately, for visualization only; training the predictor through its loss lowers Push-T success (0.92 → 0.80)

Memory

Fixed window of H frames; no KV cache or long-term memory

Speed

One world-model forward step at batch 32: 0.014 s; a full CEM plan (100 samples x 10 iterations): 15.89 s in the ICML 2025 camera-ready (App. A.6, Table 11; arXiv v2 Table 10 gave 53.0 s), both on one A6000 (authors); LeWM later measured 47 s per DINO-WM plan in its own CEM setup (hardware not stated)

Key detail

196 tokens per frame make each CEM sample a 5-step predictor rollout (released horizon 5) whose window grows from 196 to 588 tokens at H = 3, with all samples of an iteration run as one batch [D]; LeWM's one-token-per-frame design runs the same kind of plan in ~1 s (0.98 s vs 47 s in LeWM's measurement)

ICML 2025. Availability: code + weights. Overview

Dreamer-style model-based RL on object slots instead of one holistic latent. Each imagined step runs the dynamics model and the actor's SAT in sequence, with cost set by the slot count rather than the image resolution.

Representation

N = 2-10 object slots of 128-d per frame from SAVi (learned slot init, 3 Slot Attention iterations on the first frame, 1 afterwards); slots projected to 256-d tokens; frame size not stated in the text

Core

Dynamics: OCVP-Seq transformer encoder, 4 layers, d 256, 8 heads, FFN 512; in code each layer is a relational and a temporal pre-LayerNorm sub-layer, each with its own ReLU FFN. One Slot Aggregation Transformer (SAT) each for reward, value and actor: 4 causal layers, d 256, 8 heads, FFN 512, RMSNorm (SiLU FFN in code); 12M parameters in total

Attention

Dynamics (OCVP-Seq order, as in code): relational attention (the N slots plus the action token of one step) then temporal attention (each token over its own history). SAT: causal over time with ALiBi recency bias; 1 [out] + 4 [reg] tokens per step (paper; the released config uses 0 [reg]); no token can attend to earlier steps' [out]/[reg] tokens

Actions

4-D end-effector + gripper commands a_0:t are inputs to the dynamics transformer alongside the slot history (the embedding mechanism is not spelled out in the paper)

Prediction

One pass predicts all N next slots (regression): joint-embedding loss to SAVi slots of the real next frame plus image reconstruction through the SAVi decoder; no teacher forcing; S seed frames then T = 15 imagined steps

Decoder

SAVi CNN spatial-broadcast decoder: per-slot RGB + alpha masks composited by weighted sum; used in the dynamics loss and for visualisation, not by the actor

Memory

The dynamics model and SAT re-read the slot history each step (S + imagined steps); no KV cache mentioned

Speed

No inference or wall-clock figure; everything trains on one A100 40 GB (authors)

Key detail

Reward, value and actor are MLP heads on SAT [out] tokens, with symlog two-hot reward/value bins (255 over [−20, 20] in code); [D] per-step cost scales with the number of slots N, not with pixels; the actor head outputs a Gaussian (μ, σ)
