Details
Overview

An early playable real-time diffusion world model (Minecraft), released with open weights ('Oasis 500M'). A ViT autoencoder maps each 360x640 frame to an 18x32x16 latent, which the DiT patchifies into 144 tokens; the DiT generates one frame at a time with full spatial attention inside the frame and causal temporal attention over a 32-frame window, trained with Diffusion Forcing. With context keys and values cached, each pass adds only 144 new tokens, so batch-1 serving is bound by weight reads rather than by FLOPs (the open reference loop has no cache); Decart's custom kernels and multi-GPU engine behind the 20 fps demo are closed.

Representation

ViT-L/20 KL-VAE: 360x640 frame → 18x32 latent with 16 channels, no temporal compression; DiT patch 2 → 144 tokens per frame [D]

Core

DiT-S/2 (open-oasis): 16 blocks, d 1024, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4; each block = spatial attention + MLP, then temporal attention + MLP, each pair with its own adaLN; no pretrained video base named

Attention

Factorized: full (bidirectional) spatial attention over the 144 tokens of a frame; causal temporal axial attention per spatial position over up to 32 frames; axial RoPE in space, RoPE in time

Actions

25-dim action vector per frame (23 binary key/button flags, several can be on at once, plus 2 continuous camera axes in [−1, 1]) → Linear(25, 1024), added to the timestep embedding that drives the adaLN modulations

Prediction

Diffusion Forcing (independent noise level per frame), v-prediction, sigmoid beta schedule; reference sampler DDIM with 10 steps per frame, context frames held at noise level 14; the demo's step count is not disclosed

Decoder

ViT-L/20 decoder (12 layers, width 1024) → 360x640 frame, once per generated frame

Memory

Sliding window of 32 frames; no KV cache in the reference loop, so every DDIM step re-runs the whole window (up to 32 × 144 = 4,608 tokens [D]); generated latents join the window directly, with no decode and re-encode; blog lists limited long-horizon memory as a known failure

Speed

360p at 20 fps, 47 ms per frame, on NVIDIA H100s (company claim; GPUs per stream and demo checkpoint size not disclosed); the open 500M model runs at 2.58 FPS in MineWorld's Table 1 (third party, GPU not stated)

Key detail

Per-frame generation with 144-token passes: ≈0.12 TFLOP per cached pass against ≈1.2 GB of 16-bit weights (≈608M params), so single-stream decoding is weight-bandwidth-bound and batching users is the lever [D]

blog post (web technical report). Availability: code + weights. Details
Overview

An offline, multi-game world-action model: one GPT-2-style transformer over IRIS-like token sequences learns the world model (next observation tokens, reward, termination) and the Q-function at the same time, pretrained on 15 Atari games with 10M transitions each. At decision time a short beam search (horizon 2) over the model's own imagined futures corrects the Q-estimates. Beams are batched, but every imagined frame still costs 36 sequential token decodes, and planning drops throughput from 10.8 to 1.26 FPS.

Representation

VQ-VAE on 84×84 grayscale frames: 36 tokens per frame (6×6 [D]), vocabulary 2048; 3-layer CNN with self-attention at resolutions 6 and 12 (IRIS code base), frozen after stage 1

Core

GPT-2 (minGPT): JOWA-150M 12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads; JOWA-70M 6 × 768 × 12; JOWA-40M 4 × 512 × 8; dropout 0.1; input = vocabulary + position + learnable task embedding

Attention

Causal over interleaved (z_t^1..z_t^36, a_t) tokens; L = 8 steps, max 296 tokens (8 × 37 [D])

Actions

One action token per step (18-action Atari space) plus a task embedding; the Q-head reads the output at the last observation token z_t^36 of each step, the reward and done heads the action token; next-code, reward and done heads are 2-layer MLPs; the JOWA-150M Q-head is a 3-layer MLP (hidden 1,792, 3 distributional heads; 40M and 70M: 1 head, hidden 768 and 1,024) trained by TD with CQL

Prediction

Next observation token autoregressive within a frame, z_t^k | z_≤t-1, z_t^<k, a_≤t-1, so 36 serial decodes per imagined frame [D]; reward sign {-1, 0, 1} and termination as classification; distributional Q-head (3-layer MLP, hidden 1792, 3 heads for 150M) trained by TD learning

Decoder

VQ-VAE CNN decoder; decisions use only token-space heads, but the released code decodes every imagined frame during beam search (K + K² frames per action, output discarded) and turns decoded imagined frames into synthetic fine-tuning data

Memory

Context up to 8 steps = 296 tokens; with planning at most 8 − H = 6 real steps plus 2 imagined. The paper gives no cache details; the released code keeps a per-layer KV cache (prefill once, then single-token cached passes; per-beam caches concatenated for batched beam search)

Speed

JOWA-150M on 7 games: 10.8 FPS without planning, 1.26 FPS with beam search (H = 2, K = 2-4), 0.12 FPS with MCTS; hardware not stated (authors, Table 5). Pretraining 1.75M steps, 'around 12 days on A100 GPUs', GPU count not given

Key detail

Beam search calls the world model K²(H−1)+K times but takes only H forward latencies because beams are batched; at H = 2 the released code runs 1 prefill + 2 × 37 = 75 serial transformer passes per action [D]; 1.26 FPS ≈ 0.79 s per frame [D] (the paper does not say whether FPS counts decisions or emulator frames at frame skip 4)

Status and sources

ICLR 2025. Availability: code + weights. Details
Overview

An IRIS-style token world model whose transformer is replaced by a Retentive Network and whose per-token decode loop is removed. Retention keeps a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a KV cache, and Parallel Observation Prediction (POP) feeds 64 learned prediction tokens from that state to sample all 64 next-frame codes in one call. Representation

64 VQ codes per 64×64 frame (8×8 grid), vocabulary 512; VQ-GAN-style CNN tokenizer without the discriminator (IRIS uses 16 codes)

RetNet (retention, not softmax attention): 5 layers, 4 retention heads, d 256, FFN 1024, dropout 0.1; parameter count not disclosed (~4.3M block weights [D]); FFN activation GELU per the paper (A.3), SiLU in the released code

Attention

Multi-scale retention with a per-head exponential decay and relative position; chunkwise mode is parallel inside a chunk of c = 3 observation-action blocks in training (195 tokens [D]; one block at imagination) and recurrent between chunks through a 64×64 (d/h × d/h) state per head; world-model context 2 frames

Actions

One action token per step (learned embedding) after the 64 observation tokens; reward and termination are read from the action token; the world model reuses the tokenizer's embedding table

Prediction

POP: K = 64 learned prediction tokens u are run from the recurrent state S_t and all next-frame tokens are sampled in one pass; default mode = 2 sequential calls per imagined frame (state update with z_t, a_t, then prediction with u), so 2H calls over the horizon H = 10 instead of KH = 640 (Table 6)

Decoder

VQ-VAE CNN decoder for the reconstruction loss only; the actor-critic reads the token code vectors through a small CNN + LSTM, so imagination decodes no pixels

Memory

Fixed-size retention state per layer and head replaces a growing KV cache; u tokens never enter the state update

Speed

15.4× faster imagination than prior token-based world models and under 12 h of training per game (authors); run times measured on an RTX 4090 workstation, other experiments on V100s

Key detail

POP doubles the tokens per observation prediction (2K vs K, Table 6) but turns KH sequential calls into 2H; superhuman on 12 of 26 Atari 100k games (authors)

Causal over one token per step; training batch 16 x 64 steps; imagination 8 context + 16 imagined steps

Action mixer MLP (Linear-LN-ReLU-Linear-LN) fuses z_t and a_t into one d 512 token before the transformer

Prediction

One pass per imagined step; one categorical sample from the predicted next distribution; no iterative decoding

Decoder

CNN decoder trains the VAE only; the agent acts on [z_t, h_t], so no pixels are decoded in imagination

Memory

24 cached steps at batch 1024: ~100 MB as implemented (the released 'KV cache' stores each layer's input, allocated bf16 but promoted to fp32 by LayerNorm outputs; K and V are recomputed each step); a true bf16 K/V cache is also ~100 MB [D]

Speed

4.3 h per Atari 100k run on one RTX 3090; 9.3 V100-hours at 11.9 training FPS, measured on a V100 (authors); no imagination throughput reported

Key detail

1 token per step and 2 layers: ~20 MB of fp32 transformer weights plus a ~100 MB fp32 cache at 24 steps x 1024 [D]; per-step cost grows with context because K and V are recomputed

Status and sources

NeurIPS 2023. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2310.09615 Sec. 3.1-3.2 (action mixer, KV cache, agent state [z_t, h_t]); Tables 1, 5-10, 12; github.com/weipu-zhang/STORM sub_models/transformer_model.py, attention_blocks.py, world_models.py; config_files/STORM.yaml; PyTorch 2.0 AMP docs (LayerNorm autocasts to float32).

arXiv · code · SVG

Wayve · 20236.5B

Driving video tokens, decoded one at a time

Token videoread

Details
Overview

A generative world model for driving: a 6.5B causal transformer predicts the next image token over an interleaved sequence of text, image and action tokens, trained on 4,700 h of London driving. Each 288x512 frame is 576 discrete tokens from a 0.3B DINO-distilled tokenizer, so one frame costs 576 serial passes, and a separate 2.6B video diffusion U-Net, not a transformer, turns the tokens into pixels with 50 DDIM steps. The report says the model does not yet run in real time.

Representation

576 discrete tokens per 288x512 frame (18x32, downsampling 16), vocabulary 8,192, from a 0.3B image tokenizer trained with a DINO distillation loss

Core

6.5B decoder-only transformer with causal masking, width d = 4,096 (shared embedding dimension); layer and head counts not disclosed; norms, feed-forward and residual layout not described, so the diagram draws only the masked attention layer

Attention

Dense causal attention over 26 frames at 6.25 Hz (4 s): 26 x (32 text + 576 image + 2 action) = 15,860 tokens; FlashAttention v2; sliding window beyond the context

Actions

2 action tokens and 32 T5-large text tokens per step in the interleaved sequence; conditioning tokens are dropped at random in training, giving unconditional, action- and text-conditioned generation

Prediction

Next-token softmax with top-k = 50: 'n forward steps to generate one new image frame', so 576 serial passes per frame; optional classifier-free guidance doubles the evaluations [D]

Decoder

2.6B video diffusion 3D U-Net with factorized space/time attention: 50 DDIM steps per window of 7 frames (2 overlapping context frames), then temporal upsampling 6.25 → 12.5 → 25 Hz

Memory

KV-cache policy not disclosed; context capped at 26 frames with a sliding window for longer rollouts

Speed

Not disclosed; generation 'does not yet run at real-time' (authors). Training: world model 15 days on 64 A100-80GB, tokenizer 4 days on 32, decoder 15 days on 32 = ~1,568 A100-days [D]

Key detail

576 dependent decode steps per frame through 6.5B parameters, then a 50-step diffusion decoder; with 16-bit weights (precision not disclosed) each step reads 13 GB of weights [D], so decoding at batch 1 is bandwidth-bound

Status and sources

company technical report. Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2309.17080 Sec. 2.1-2.4 (tokens, world model, decoder), Sec. 4.1-4.3 (sizes, training), Sec. 5.1-5.2 (sampling, DDIM), Sec. 9 (not real time).

arXiv · SVG

UC San Diego · 202333B

Frozen LLM as world model inside tree search

LLM & coderead

Details
Overview

Uses an off-the-shelf LLM as a world model. A frozen LLaMA-33B is prompted three ways: as the policy that proposes actions, as the world model that writes the next state in natural language, and as the reward model. Monte Carlo tree search runs 10-20 iterations over these text states before one answer is committed. Every tree expansion costs several 33B LLM calls (action proposals, next-state generation, reward scoring) inside a sequential search loop, with no training at all.

Representation

A state is natural-language text: the block configuration (Blocksworld), the values of intermediate variables (GSM8k) or the current fact (PrOntoQA); an action is a text step (a block move, a sub-question, a rule)

Core

LLaMA-33B used frozen with prompts (60 layers, d 6656, 52 heads, 32.5B; LLaMA paper Table 2); the same model serves as policy, world model and reward model; Llama-2 70B in the full-Blocksworld experiment

Attention

Ordinary causal LLM attention over prompt (in-context demonstrations + state) and generated text; each generation is cut at 2,048 tokens or a newline

Actions

Text in the prompt: the world model is queried with (state, action) and writes the next state; the policy samples d candidate actions per expansion

Prediction

Sampled next-token decoding at temperature 0.8; one LLM generation per transition in Blocksworld and PrOntoQA, several sampled answers per transition in GSM8k; rewards from action log-probability, answer confidence (share of the most frequent sampled answer) and the probability of 'Yes' to 'Is this reasoning step correct?'

Decoder

None; states are text

Memory

The MCTS tree stores text states and Q-values; reward prompts hide the history and feed only the current state

Speed

No latency figure; all experiments on 4× NVIDIA A5000 24 GB (authors). Per iteration: d expansions × (action proposal + next-state generation + reward) plus a roll-out to a terminal state [D: structural, from Algorithm 1]; the log-prob and 'Yes' rewards are single scoring passes, not decodes (released code)

Key detail

RAP(20) with LLaMA-33B solves 42% of 6-step Blocksworld tasks vs 40% for GPT-4 CoT; cost grows with iterations × depth × branching [D: Algorithm 1 loops]

Status and sources

EMNLP 2023. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2305.14992 Sec. 3.1-3.3 (world model, rewards, MCTS), Sec. 4.1 (LLaMA-33B, T 0.8), Table 1; arXiv 2305.14992 App. A (MCTS changes), App. B.1-B.2 (decoding limit, 4× A5000), Algorithm 1; LLaMA arXiv 2302.13971 Sec. 2 and Table 2 (33B config); LLaMA v1 model.py; llm-reasoners code: examples/rap_gsm8k/world_model.py, reasoners/lm/llama_model.py.

arXiv · code · SVG

University of Toronto · 2022size not disclosed

Transformer over object slots, one pass per frame

Object-centricread

Details
Overview

An object-centric dynamics model. A frozen SAVi (or STEVE) encoder turns each frame into a handful of object slots, and a small transformer encoder over the slots of the last T frames predicts all of the next frame's slots in one pass, then rolls out autoregressively. There are no actions; rollouts feed video prediction, VQA and PHYRE planning. The transformer sees only tens of tokens per step, so the encoder and the per-slot spatial-broadcast decoder carry most of the compute.

Representation

N object slots per frame from a frozen SAVi (STEVE on Physion): 6-8 slots of 128-d (192-d on Physion) at 64×64 or 128×128; a linear layer maps slots to d_e = 128 (OBJ3D) or 256

Core

BERT-style Pre-LN transformer encoder: N_T = 4 layers on OBJ3D and CLEVRER, 8 on Physion and PHYRE; 8 heads; FFN 4×d_e; parameter count not disclosed (~3M block weights for 4 layers at d 256 [D]); ReLU FFN, dropout 0.1 in the official code (PyTorch TransformerEncoderLayer defaults)

Attention

Full bidirectional self-attention over the T×N slot tokens of the history; temporal-only sinusoidal positional encoding so slots of one frame share it (permutation equivariant); T = 6 burn-in frames on OBJ3D and CLEVRER (6 × 7 = 42 tokens on CLEVRER [D]), 15 on Physion, 1 on PHYRE

Actions

None; unconditional video prediction, with VQA and PHYRE task-success readouts on the rollouts

Prediction

One pass predicts all N next-frame slots jointly: the last N outputs go through a linear layer (the paper adds a residual from the current slots; the official code has none), L2 slot loss (+ image loss); K = 10 rollout frames, predictions fed back

Decoder

Frozen SAVi spatial-broadcast CNN decoder (8×8 broadcast grid on OBJ3D and CLEVRER, 16×16 on PHYRE) renders each slot as RGB plus alpha mask; STEVE's transformer decoder on Physion

Memory

Sliding history of T frames = T×N tokens; no KV cache (bidirectional encoder)

Speed

No inference figure; 'can be trained on servers with 4 modern GPUs in less than 5 days' (authors)

Key detail

42 tokens per step (CLEVRER) through a 4-layer encoder: the quadratic attention core is ~3% of a step's MACs [D]; the SAVi encoder and per-slot decoder dominate

Status and sources

ICLR 2023. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2210.05861 Sec. 3.2-3.3 (architecture, training), Sec. 4.5 ablations (N_T, T, K, P.E.); arXiv 2210.05861 App. C Table 8 (per-dataset N, D_slot, D_e, N_T, T, K), App. C text (8 heads, FFN 4×, Pre-LN, 16×16 broadcast on PHYRE); Reproducibility statement (4 GPUs, < 5 days); github.com/pairlab/SlotFormer (code and weights); Official code video_prediction/models/slotformer.py and configs slotformer_{obj3d,clevrer,phyre}_params.py; SAVi, arXiv 2111.12594 (8×8 spatial broadcast decoder).

TU Dortmund · 202219M

Transformer-XL over three tokens per step

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

A Dreamer-style agent whose dynamics model is a causal Transformer-XL instead of an RNN. A CNN VAE turns each 64x64 observation into 32x32 categorical latents; latent, action and reward enter as three separate tokens per step, and the hidden state read from the action token drives MLP heads for the next latent, reward and discount. The policy acts from z_t alone, so the transformer runs only in training and imagination, where the XL memory doubles throughput to 39,000 samples/s on one A100.

Representation

32 categorical variables x 32 classes per step from a CNN VAE on 64x64 grayscale frames (stack of 4)

Core

Transformer-XL: 10 layers, d 256, 4 heads of 64, FFN 1024, SiLU; dynamics model 10.8M, world model 19M (Table 5); post-LN, LayerNorm after each residual add (code)

Attention

Causal with relative positions; history 16 steps = 3ℓ−1 = 47 tokens per the paper [D] (50 in the released code), plus Transformer-XL segment memory

Actions

Own action token through a modality-specific linear embedding; h_t is read from the action token's output

Prediction

One pass per imagined step; MLP heads give the next latent (categorical sample), reward (mean) and discount

Decoder

CNN decoder trains the VAE only; the policy is conditioned on z_t, so nothing is decoded in imagination

Memory

Cached XL segment outputs: imagination 39,000 samples/s with the memory vs 19,900 with a vanilla transformer (~2x) [D]

Speed

Imagination 39,000 samples/s on one A100 at batch 400 and ~10 h per Atari run (authors); policy 653 frames/s on a CPU

Key detail

3 tokens per step, against 1 in STORM and 17 in IRIS; the transformer is never needed at deployment

Status and sources

ICLR 2023. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2303.07109 Sec. 2.1 (tokens, Transformer-XL), Table 4 (hyperparameters), Table 5 (parameters), App. A.1 (wall-clock); Official code github.com/jrobine/twm: twm/nets.py (post-LN block, token count), twm/config.py; OpenReview TdBaDGCpjly (ICLR 2023 submission, Sep 2022); STORM arXiv 2310.09615 Sec. 2, Table 1 (comparison).

University of Geneva · 2022~30M

GPT over VQ codes, one token at a time

RL world modelverified

Details
Overview

The archetype of the token-level world model for reinforcement learning. A VQ-VAE turns each 64x64 Atari frame into 16 discrete codes, and a small GPT predicts the next frame's codes one token at a time, together with reward and termination. The agent is trained entirely inside this imagination. Each imagined frame costs 17 dependent transformer passes, which is the cost later designs attack.

Representation

16 VQ codes per 64x64 frame, vocabulary 512 (VQGAN autoencoder without the discriminator)

Core

GPT-2-style causal transformer: 10 layers, d 256, 4 heads (minGPT)

Attention

Causal over all tokens; context 20 steps = 340 tokens; KV cache reset at 340 tokens

Actions

One action token between frames

Prediction

Next-token softmax; 17 single-token passes per frame (1 action + 16 codes); reward and termination are read from the action token

Decoder

VQ-VAE CNN decoder; the actor-critic reads decoded frames, so it runs during imagination

Memory

Full causal context, ~3.5 MB of KV per sequence in fp16 [D]

Speed

No inference figure reported; ~3.5 A100-days of training per game (authors)

Key detail

Mean human-normalized score 1.046 on Atari 100k; 17 serial passes per frame

Status and sources

ICLR 2023 (oral, notable top 5%). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2209.00588 App. A, Tables 3-4, 6; github.com/eloialonso/iris src/models/world_model.py, transformer.py, config/world_model/default.yaml; github.com/eloialonso/iris world_model_env.py (17 passes); DIAMOND arXiv 2405.12399 Table 4 (30M count).

arXiv · code · SVG

Rutgers / KAIST · 2021size not disclosed

Dreamer with a transformer in place of the GRU

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

The first transformer-based model-based RL agent (authors' claim), in the Dreamer setting. The Transformer State-Space Model (TSSM) replaces the RSSM's GRU: the deterministic state h_t is a causal transformer over the past stochastic latents and actions, one token per step, and the posterior drops h_t so every step trains in parallel. Everything else is DreamerV2: CNN encoder and decoder, discrete latents, reward and discount heads, actor-critic in imagination. The transformer is small: 2 layers in the DMC/Atari runs, 6 in the Hidden Order tasks and the released Atari config. The released code re-runs it over the whole window (up to 49 steps) for every imagined step, with no KV cache, so the cost of every layer grows with the imagined history.

Representation

DreamerV2 CNN encoder; posterior q(z_t | x_t) computed from the frame alone (no h_t), discrete stochastic latent; full state is the concatenation [h_t, z_t]

Core

TSSM per App. A.3 (DMC, Atari): 2-layer transformer, 10 heads, attention and MLP hidden size 200 (DMC) or 600 (Atari), no dropout, gating or identity-map reordering (except Atari Pong); ~0.5M (DMC) to ~4.3M (Atari) block weights [D]. App. A.4 (Hidden Order Discovery): 6 layers with identity-map reordering. Released Atari config: 6 pre-LN layers, d_model 600, 8 heads x 64, FFN 1024, dropout 0.1; ~14.8M block weights [D]. Residual layout from the code: x + LN(f(x)) without reordering (drawn), x + f(LN(x)) with it

Attention

Causal over past steps: h_t = transformer(z_{1:t-1}, a_{1:t-1}); relative positional embedding (Transformer-XL style) is a tunable option; sequence length per DreamerV2 config

Actions

One token per step: the flattened one-hot z_t is concatenated with a_t, projected by Linear + ELU to d_model, plus a sinusoidal position embedding (released code; the paper does not describe it)

Prediction

Prior p(z_t | h_t) sampled and fed back; 1 transformer pass per imagined step; image, reward and discount predictors read (h_t, z_t); ELBO with KL(q(z_t|x_t) || p(z_t|h_t))

Decoder

DreamerV2 CNN decoder from (h_t, z_t), used for the reconstruction loss and visualisation only

Memory

Attends over the whole (z, a) history: the 50-step training sequence; in imagination, context plus imagined steps (up to a 49-step window in the released code), re-run in full every step with no KV cache (code). Transformer memory limits imagination to K = 3 trajectories per sample (DMC, Atari; Sec. 3.2, App. A.3); App. A.4 and the released code start one rollout per sequence from a random state

Speed

No wall-clock or throughput figure; hardware not stated. On DMC and Atari it reaches returns comparable to Dreamer but is 'slower to saturate in general' (authors, Sec. 5.5); in the Hidden Order Discovery tasks it imagines from one random start state until the trajectory's max step (App. A.4)

Key detail

One token per step (z_t and a_t fused by Linear + ELU in the code); the myopic posterior q(z_t | x_t), without h_t, is what lets the transformer compute h_1:T for all steps in one parallel pass (Sec. 3.1)

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v2 Nov 2024). Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2202.09481 Sec. 3.1 and Table 1 (TSSM components), Sec. 3.2 (prioritized replay, K imagined trajectories); arXiv 2202.09481 App. A.3 (2 layers, 10 heads, hidden 200/600, no gating/dropout, K = 3), Fig. 6 (rollout); arXiv 2202.09481 App. A.4 (Hidden Order Discovery: 6 layers, identity-map reordering, one random start); Official code github.com/changchencc/TransDreamer: src/model/transformer.py, src/model/modules_transformer.py, src/config_files/configs_atari.py; OpenReview ICLR 2022 submission s3K0arSRl4d (first public release, Oct 2021); DreamerV2 config referenced in App. A.3 (github.com/danijar/dreamerv2) for encoder/decoder and latent type.

arXiv · code · SVG

UC Berkeley · 2021size not disclosed

GPT over binned states, actions and rewards

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

Offline RL as one big sequence-modeling problem: every state dimension, action dimension, the reward and the reward-to-go are discretized into 100 bins and become separate tokens of a small GPT. There is no learned encoder and no policy network; acting is beam search over the model's own trajectory predictions, extended one token at a time. Latency scales with state dimensionality, and the authors note it can take seconds per action, which, they say, precludes real-time control for most dynamical systems.

Representation

Each of the N state and M action dimensions, the reward and the reward-to-go is one token: per-dimension uniform or quantile discretization into V = 100 bins; input vocabulary V × (N + M + 2), output logits over V

Core

GPT-style decoder: 4 layers, 4 heads, token embedding d 128, dropout 0.1; parameter count not disclosed (~12·4·128² ≈ 0.8M block weights if the MLP is 4× wide [D])

Attention

Causal, with every reward-to-go token masked out as a key (official code); context 5 transitions of (s, a, r, R), at most 5 × (N + M + 2) − 1 tokens, e.g. 124 for a 17-D state and 6-D action [D]; training uses 10-transition sequences (code)

Actions

Action dimensions are ordinary tokens in the stream, decoded after the state tokens of the same step

Prediction

Next-token softmax, one token per pass, teacher-forced training; planning = beam search, horizon 15 transitions, observations decoded greedily (k_obs 1); paper (App. E): width 256, actions from the top 20 tokens; released code: 128 beams × 2 expansions, actions sampled after dropping the least likely tokens holding 60% of the mass (cdf_act 0.6); offline RL ranks transitions by reward plus reward-to-go instead of log-probability

Decoder

None; states are discretized scalars, decoded back by bin centres

Memory

Fixed context of 5 transitions; no KV-cache details given

Speed

'Up to multiple seconds for action selection when the context window grows too large', hardware not stated (authors, Sec. 5); training 6-12 h per model on one V100 for 80 epochs (authors, App. A)

Key detail

Per executed action: 15 × (N + M + 2) − N sequential single-token decodes (the current state is given and the last state is not sampled), e.g. 358 for HalfCheetah at horizon 15 [D]; code batches 256 rows for action and reward tokens, 128 for state tokens; a latency-bound ~1.5M-parameter workload [D]

Status and sources

NeurIPS 2021. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2106.02039 Sec. 3.1 (tokenization, 4 layers/4 heads), Sec. 3.2 (beam search, reward-to-go), Algorithm 1, Sec. 5 (seconds per action); arXiv 2106.02039 App. A (d 128, dropout 0.1, V100 6-12 h), App. E (beam width 256, horizon 15, V 100, context 5, k_obs, k_act); Official code jannerm/trajectory-transformer: trajectory/models/transformers.py (pre-norm blocks, GELU MLP, R-to-go key mask, position embedding), trajectory/search/core.py and sampling.py (beam plan, cdf filter), config/offline.py, scripts/train.py, README (hyperparameters differ from paper); Environment dimensions for the [D] examples: D4RL HalfCheetah (17-D state, 6-D action).

arXiv · code · page · SVG

About

Architecture diagrams for world models whose dynamics model or generative backbone is a transformer, drawn in one visual language after the LLM Architecture Gallery. Numbers marked [D] in the details are our own arithmetic; speeds are the developers' own figures on their own hardware.

Corrections and new models are welcome as issues or pull requests.

Changelog

2026-10-23 (version 6): only what a source states

  • Diagrams now draw only what a source states. The 38 elements that no source states were removed: guessed norms, feed-forward layers and residual lines in AAPT, comma.ai, GAIA-1, GAIA-2 and Genie, invented steps (a KV-cache write, a codebook lookup, a denoising update), the SwiGLU inset in Dreamer 4, and the decoder and sampling loop of the long-context SSM model.
  • A block whose remaining layers are undisclosed shows one plain "Rest of block not stated" box, and its facts name the missing parts.
  • Dreamer 4 keeps its pre-norm residual layout: the paper starts from "a standard transformer with pre-layer RMSNorm, RoPE, and SwiGLU".
  • The dashed-outline style is gone, the Source check panel reports removed elements, and the renderer warns about any element tagged `assumed`.

2026-10-23 (version 5): source audit

  • Every card was cross-checked against its primary sources in three independent passes: 2,340 elements over 49 cards, 440 of them corrected. Examples: IRIS adds its learned positions at the token embedding and its transformer has about 8.5M parameters (30M is the whole agent); Dreamer 4 runs causal time attention in one layer of four and has a reward head; WorldPlay has no cross-attention in the released code; Matrix-Game 2.0's real-time model has 1.62B parameters.
  • Each box records its basis: stated in the paper, shown in the released code or config, or assumed. Assumed boxes are drawn with a dashed outline, and each card gains a *Source check* panel with its counts.
  • Sources lists name primary sources only.
  • The renderer now splits an arrow into a nested fanout to each of its boxes.
  • `data.json` no longer carries the unaudited token-square `diagram` spec, and the legacy token-square SVGs were removed from `docs/`.

2026-10-22 (version 4)

  • Redesigned page: centered title block with crop marks over a faint engineering grid, monospace labels and figures, diagrams on blueprint-grid tiles, a sticky search and filter bar, more whitespace throughout.
  • The full-page viewer shows each diagram once (no duplicate title) and both models' details when comparing.
  • Plain backgrounds: the grid behind the page, the diagram tiles and the viewer was removed.

2026-10-22 (version 3)

  • New page design: small two-column cards with a compact diagram, name and one-line tagline; facts fold behind *Details*, one fact at a time.
  • Clicking a diagram opens the detailed version full-page, with zoom, previous and next (arrow keys), and a side-by-side compare.
  • Diagram text cut to the essentials: at most 6 annotations of at most 44 characters, short box labels; caveats moved into the facts. The renderer enforces these limits.
  • New compact thumbnail mode (`--stack --mini`); every card has a `tagline`.

2026-10-21 (version 2)

  • Every card now leads with a bottom-up stack diagram in the style of the LLM Architecture Gallery: small boxes with one label each, repeated blocks with an N × marker, residual skip lines into ⊕, side inputs, zoom-in insets, and all numbers in annotations outside the model.
  • New renderer `wmgallery/stack.py` with a condensed mode for slides; specs live in `MODEL["flow"]` (see `docs/FLOW.md`).
  • The renderer checks every leader line and warns when one crosses a box; all 49 diagrams pass.
  • The earlier token-square card stays available under each diagram as a compact summary.

2026-10-21

  • First release: cards for the models covered by the "Transformer-based world models" research (RL world models, discrete-token video models, causal diffusion transformers, driving and robot models, embedding predictors, world-action models, LLM, object-centric and SSM designs).
  • Renderer: one declarative spec per model produces the web card (SVG) and a compact slide card (PNG).

Guide

How to read a diagram

Data flows from the bottom up: input, encoder, the transformer block, the sampling loop, output heads, decoder. Click a card's diagram to open the detailed version; open Details for the facts behind it.

  • one operation
  • attention (the label names the mask)
  • encoder, tokenizer or decoder
  • action or conditioning module
  • repeated block, with its N × marker
  • + residual add
  • zoom-in on one box
  • rollout loop: the label names what carries to the next step (tokens, latents)
  • 12 numbers sit beside the model
  • "Rest of block not stated": layers the source does not describe

Evidence: verified facts passed a 3-vote adversarial check; read facts come from the paper or code; claim facts come from a developer page only. Keys: / search, ← → previous and next, Esc close.
